#1851. Steven Pressley answers Dundee resignation question after Hearts thrashing - but no Hibs appeal planned

Steven Pressley did not consider quitting in the wake of Dundee suffering their biggest-ever home defeat against Hearts on Saturday night.

The 8-0 loss led the manager to take full blame afterwards. He said he wanted to “crawl under a rock and hide” following such a landmark reversal.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 53-year-old has had little time to ponder his future. Dundee are back in action as soon as Tuesday night at Easter Road against Hibs, who are themselves hurting following a 4-0 home defeat against Dundee United in their last outing. "It has been a tough 24, 48 hours," said Pressley. "There’s a lot of embarrassment, a lot of disappointment."

He stressed there was also a determination to learn from the most challenging experience of his managerial career. Although he has spoken before of coming close to walking away on at least two occasions last season, resigning had not crossed his mind this time.

“Not this weekend, no,” he said. “I've had to find strength from I don't know where, but not this weekend. Not this weekend. But it was hugely embarrassing.

“It probably ranks as the most embarrassing moment of my managerial career thus far.

“I'm 17, 18 years into my coaching career and it's why, in football, you can never become complacent.

“Because nothing ever surprises you. You think you've lived through everything, and then something else comes along. And very much that was Saturday.”

Pressley has admitted considering quitting after disappointing results in his first season at Dundee, one of which was a 4-0 defeat at Pittodrie against Aberdeen. Dundee recovered from a poor start to the campaign and Pressley succeeded in getting his critics firmly on side.

However, the historic nature of Saturday’s result meant he found himself under fire again from some quarters. Pressley has resolved to find the answers. Dundee will be without key defender Owen Bevan, who was sent off on Saturday night, against Hibs.

The club have decided against appealing the decision. “We accept the punishment,” said Pressley. “It is not ideal but I don’t think there was a real chance of it being overturned.”

Pressley suggested there would not be a radical overhaul of the side or system. “It is difficult to change a lot in two days so we have to be very careful," he said. "But we have thought a lot about what we can do. There has to be a change in (the suspended) Owen Bevan. There is a lot to consider. But the most important thing is we give a response and try to get some level of pride back.”

By Matthew Cooper | 22 Nov 2026 12:45

Charlton Athletic will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Lincoln City to The Valley on Tuesday evening.

Charlton are in the midst of a woeful run of form, having won just one of their last 13 Championship matches to leave them six points above the relegation zone.

#1848. Nightmare at Dens Park: Dundee come to terms with history as child asks ‘what about last night?’

It wasn’t quite the morning after the night before. Nevertheless, Dundee players were very obviously still bearing the mental scars on Monday nearly 48 hours after a night of infamy inflicted by Hearts.

An old adage is that it’s best to go again as quickly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“To a point, yes…” agreed Steven Pressley when this theory was put to him at the sun-sprayed Dundee training facility at Gardyne College Campus ahead of Tuesday’s return to action against Hibs.

The counter argument, one the Dundee manager was clearly conscious of, is that three nights later is maybe just a bit too soon. In addition, when it comes to grounds Dundee might choose to visit for their next assignment after losing 8-0 – or should that be 0-8 – then Easter Road would not be high on the list. Dundee have not won there for a quarter of a century. The record books are being well-thumbed just now.

“We obviously don’t have a lot of time to work on elements of our game plan,” said Pressley. “It has been pretty frantic.

“Not only have we had to plan how we have to play and be prepared for Hibernian, I have also had to think a lot about the management of the group and everybody within that. I have had to find a way to stabilise the group.”

The employment of such words as “stabilise” reflect the harrowing nature of the experience. A group of 16 players including substitutes, many of them in their early 20s, endured something akin to a medical procedure.

A rampant Hearts side removed their sense of self-belief with almost surgical precision. Professional sport is often about how quickly such wounds can heal.

But this is new territory for everyone, including those as steeped in the game as Pressley. Owen Goodman, the 22-year-old keeper on loan from Crystal Palace, was perhaps left with most to feel sore about on Saturday night as goal after goal whizzed past him.

Dundee presumably have a duty of care towards him. It’s maybe one reason why Pressley decided against showing a re-run of the match the following morning. “I didn’t think putting them through the agony of watching it again was helpful,” he said.

Goodman was the last Dundee player to leave the field and one of the first in on Monday. He mentioned never having let in eight goals before, even in academy games. This was new territory for so many.

Young men such as Goodman carry a huge burden of responsibility as they attempt to bounce back from a historic defeat. An updated edition of the definitive Dundee FC history book, They Wore the Dark Blue, has just been published. It’s already out of date in one respect. Although it contains every result, competitive and otherwise, dating back to 1893, the Dundee fans' bible doesn’t include what now stands as the club’s biggest-ever home loss.

Such landmark results usually belong in the late 1800s, rendered a curiosity rather than a wounding detail due to the passage of time.

In Dundee’s case, prior to Saturday, their biggest-ever home defeat was relatively recent – 1971, against a Celtic side who had been crowned European champions in recent enough memory for one newspaper to describe them having “conjured the magic of Lisbon” at Dens Park following their 8-1 win.

Aberdeen equalled the margin of victory if not the scoreline in 2017. But Hearts outdid both those results on Saturday night. When Stuart Findlay rose like Alan Gilzean to nod in No 8 with a minute or so of the game left, the old pillars in the Dens Park main stand might have warped a fraction in recognition of the goal’s significance. Even if few, least of all Findlay, were probably aware of it at the time. A historic low dating back to 1893 – 1899 in the case of Dens Park itself – had been recorded.

Extraordinary, unthinkable results do happen. Just ask Hearts. Five goals down to Falkirk at home just a few weeks ago, they at least rallied to 5-2. Rallying was something Dundee conspicuously failed to do, which might have been the most disappointing aspect of the night for Pressley personally. He shouldered the blame himself, citing his suspicion that a poor performance had been in the post. He just didn't realise how poor. When he sought to rectify things at half time by sending on three substitutes there was precious little reaction. If anything things got worse, with Dundee reduced to ten men due to Owen Bevan’s red card.

Often teams who rack up handsome half-time leads cannot maintain such intensity in the second half due to a combination of factors, including stiff resolve from the opposition to avoid further embarrassment. This wasn’t evident on Saturday. Hearts scored another four goals to match their first-half quota and might have scored more, with another chalked off for a handball.

Although he says he did not consider tendering his resignation, it’s safe to assume Pressley endured a long dark night of the soul on Saturday night when he returned home to Edinburgh.

He said he found strength “from I don’t know where” and has been buoyed from a raft of messages of support. Perhaps Drey Wright, the Dundee wing-back, got to the heart of what it all meant on a human level.

“My six-year-old was at home watching the game, getting very upset with every goal that's going in,” said the 30-year-old.

“My eight-year-old is putting his hand on the shoulder of my wife, kind of subconsciously helping her out. So that's not easy to hear.

“I was back in training yesterday and later I was at the dinner table and my eldest says: ‘So Dad, what about that score last night?’ And it’s this kind of a back-to-reality moment. There’s no getting away from it.”

#1847. MN: Eyes on Manchester – the City and United duo Milan want to bring back to Italy

AC Milan are looking for opportunities to bolster the squad ahead of next season, with a particular eye on the north of England.

According to MilanNews, Milan are eyeing Manchester for the January transfer window, but also for next summer. The directors are currently in a phase of monitoring certain situations that could develop later, to their benefit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri are also interested in players whose contracts are expiring within the next 18 months, as was the case with Mario Gila this summer, who signed for the Diavolo one year before his contract with Lazio expires.

Bruno Fernandes is one to watch for the upcoming summer transfer window, with his contract expiring in June 2027 but with an option to extend. United’s attempts to extend his deal have so far been unsuccessful, likely due to the player’s desire to try something else.

Fernandes has played at an incredible level in the Premier League in recent years, winning Player of the Year for 2025-26. So far, he has made 341 official appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists.

He’s a key player for the Portuguese national team and he would provide leadership that the squad could lose if players like Luka Modric leave. Moreover, his past in Italy – where he had spells at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria – could help him integrate more quickly and effectively.

Fernandes also shares the same agency as Ruben Amorim. The relationship between the two is excellent, and already this summer the Rossoneri had inquired about a possible move for the former Sporting star.

At the other Manchester club, however, there’s an old acquaintance of Italian football who could come back into fashion as early as January: Mateo Kovacic. His contract also expires at the end of the campaign, and he could come in to add depth too.

Given the increasingly certain departure of youngster Christian Comotto, an experienced player like Kovacic – at the right price, in terms of wages – could be useful for Amorim. His situation is being watched, but there will be competition from other clubs, likely in Italy too.

#1846. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#1845. Winterton named as interim Eastbourne Town boss after Macdonald’s controversial sacking

The club stalwart has been put in temporary chatge at The Saffrons while the club look for a permanent replacement for Macdonald, whose axing alongside assistant Ben Davis has provoked an angry reaction from many fans and seen some players leave – includihg one who’d only rejoined the club on Friday.

The latest development at the Isthmian South East club came on Monday evening, when a club statement said: “To serve for an interim period, Eastbourne Town F.C are pleased to announce the appointment of popular club stalwart Dave Winterton as First Team Manager.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"Dave is, of course, very well known to most people in the local area for his long and distinguished playing, coaching and management career with our club, and we sincerely thank him for agreeing to take on this role.

"During this time, Dave will be assisted by one of our experienced senior players, Arron Hopkinson. Our thanks also go to him.

"We hope that supporters will get behind Dave and the team during this period of transition, starting this coming Saturday away at Erith Town, whilst the search for a permanent successor to Jude Macdonald continues.”

Dave is a second generation Winterton at Eastbourne Town – his father Derek played as a defender for the club in the 1950s.

He was club manager between June 2001 and January 2005, taking Town, who were playing in Division 2 of the Sussex League, into Division 1 and winning the Sussex Intermediate Cup. In 2020 Dave became the Goalkeeper coach for the club.

The move to make him interim boss comes after the surprise news on Saturday evening that Macdonald had been sacked with Town one off the bottom of the division but after two brighter league performances that had seen a point taken from each of two clashes with Sheppey and Whitstable.

Town’s statement on Saturday said: “Eastbourne Town FC have today parted company with First Team Manager Jude Macdonald and Ben Davis.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and Ben for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting new arrivals, just two years later launched an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish Runners-Up and then win the League Play-off Final.

"They then successfully kept the Club in the Isthmian F.L for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

"The club wish them both all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”

A number of Town fans have taken to social media to condemn Macdonald’s removal, calling it shocking and disgraceful.

At least a couple of players have left – including James Waters, who Macdonald had re-signed for the club only at the end of last week.

#1844. Why the Women’s World Cup is coming to Scotland at exactly the right time

Hot on the heels of the launch of the Scottish government’s ‘Project 2035’ drive to make Scotland a leading force in women’s football comes the news that Scotland will host Women’s World Cup games during that same year.

The tournament, to be jointly staged with England, Northern Ireland and Wales, will see games played at Hampden Park and Easter Road in Edinburgh. So girls dreaming of footballing glory can now add the spine-tingling Hampden roar to imagined wondergoals.

#1843. Burgess Hill Town youngsters are flying – and Byrne scores 15 goals in two games

The team had to settle for a point after Rovers striker Matty Fanimo hit a stunner to bring the scores level at 2-2.

In isolation a point on the road is perfectly acceptable, but Mansell was feeling the effect of six league games without a win – and now 15 games without a win on grass.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His team are quietly working their way down the table, occupying 15th place.

Buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. The winning goal was a very scrappy affair ending with three Hillian defenders on their backsides as Alfie Cerulli bundled home from a yard.

Mansell was quite direct in his post-match interview after that loss, saying: “Gutted, it’s a familiar pill to swallow, there wasn’t enough desire in both boxes.”

There were raised blood pressures among fan walking away from the MTC that evening and a mixed bag of social media comments.

Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent new facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben said: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”

Hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”

I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

Striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He quickly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

After the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”

Bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

Mansell is acutely aware of this so will be looking for a win when title contenders Eastbourne Borough travel to the MTC on Saturday afternoon. Three points at this time would be huge.

#1842. Portsmouth vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 22 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:06

West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.

The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.

Portsmouth are sitting four points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing five and losing five of their 16 league games this term.

Pompey put together a six-game unbeaten run before they fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat in their most recent home outing before the international break.

John Mousinho's side then returned to action with an underwhelming display in Saturday's 1-1 away draw against Bolton Wanderers, which saw Josh Murphy score the opener with what proved to be Pompey's only shot on target.

Murphy's first goal since March 2025 was soon called out by Sam Dalby as Portsmouth played out a third consecutive away draw after previously taking a point from trips to Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley.

Portsmouth will now return to the familiar surroundings of Fratton Park, where they have won four of their last six outings since losing their opening two home games.

That said, they will be looking to tighten up their backline if they are to take anything off the league's highest scorers, having recorded just one clean sheet in their eight outings at Fratton Park

Meanwhile, West Ham have significant work to do if they are to secure an immediate return to the Premier League in their first Championship campaign since 2011-12.

The West Ham hierarchy took the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after being underwhelmed by a return of six wins from the opening 13 league matches of the season.

Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken over the reins, but he is still waiting to secure his first win after over two draws and one defeat in his first three matches.

After starting his reign with a comeback 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, Parker saw his side fall to a narrow 2-1 loss against Blackburn Rovers, before his charges returned from the international break with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Championship's basement side Preston North End.

As a result, West Ham have now gone five games without a win since recording back-to-back away victories over Lincoln City and Swansea City, leaving them three points adrift of the playoff spots and eight points away from the top two.

In search of inspiration, the Hammers can take confidence from the fact they have already beaten Portsmouth at home in the EFL Cup this season, and have won two of their previous three head-to-head away games - a 4-1 success in December 2008 (a game that Parker started) and a 1-0 victory in January 2012.

Portsmouth’s lengthy absentee list features Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Benjamin Arthur and Connor Ogilvie.

Jayden Meghoma is a doubt after being forced off in the closing stages against Bolton with an ankle problem, while a calf issue prevented Marlon Pack from starting Saturday’s draw.

Mousinho will welcome back midfielder Ebou Adams, who has served his one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Kyle Walker-Peters and Keiber LaMadrid due to muscle and knee problems respectively.

Goalkeeper Alphonse Areola remains a doubt after sitting out Saturday’s draw with an injury he sustained in the pre-match warm-up against Blackburn earlier this month.

Defender Max Kilman is expected to come into the back four after completing his one-match suspension for accumulating five yellow cards in the Championship.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Adams, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Kamara; Shade

However, we think they will be forced to settle for a point against a Portsmouth side that has lost just one of their previous eight matches.

#1840. GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s plans.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

#1839. Bradford City boss Michael Duff issues Barnsley FC warning ahead of another League One derby

Without a win in 10 league games since September 2 and in their worst league position for many a year, the Oakwell outfit look like being in the thick of a survival fight for the rest of the season and face the very real prospect of fourth-tier football next term for the first time since 1978-79 if their fortunes don't turn around in the new year.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It's a far cry from their highs in their one season under Duff in 2022-23 when they reached the play-off final and went desperately close to promotion back to the Championship.

Duff, who was at Oakwell to watch his old club take on Sheffield Wednesday on Friday - the hosts lost 2-1, the margin of defeat for their past five league losses - said: "Barnsley didn't look like a wounded animal on Friday, but a football team with loads of energy and good players.

"I don't think we're at a point now where we can assume that, well: 'we're just better than them'. Everything that's got us, this football club, the team, the squad, to where it has and the success it's had, is because it's had that underdog mentality. What we can't have is we slip into 'oh, we're better than them'.. Because that's when trouble starts, isn't it?

"I watched them on Friday against Sheffield Wednesday and they should have got some out of the game.

"Barnsley found themselves 2-0 down and then were really, really good for the rest of the game.

"It's not like the Premier League where you very rarely see teams at the bottom of the league beat the teams at the top. In this league, it happens all the time.

“Bromley have beaten Reading, Peterborough have beaten Plymouth. It's not a league where you (think) we’ll beat them or ‘two home games, we’ll win them’.

"Our lads' mentality and attitude is pretty good. I don't think we have that sort of arrogance in terms of ‘we'll be alright, we'll just win today.’

"They know what they have to do, they know the effort they have to put in, the application, the energy they have to put into every game and since I've been here they've done that every game.

"They did it before we came and, like I said, they just nicked a couple early in the season. We've done enough where we should have won them and we haven't quite nicked them."

City are on a run of nine matches in just under a month in four different competitions and they face midweek games for the next four matches. Tonight is also their final game of a six-match run of fixtures at Valley Parade.

Duff continued: "There are games that are coming now.

"There’s no way there is going to be the same 11 players on Tuesday or the following Saturday or the following Tuesday or the following Saturday.

"We’ll wrap a few up that we need to and there will be opportunities for people.

"The good thing with competition is they know they’ll get opportunities so they need to be ready. If you get given a chance and you don’t take it, it might not come around again so quickly.

"That’s when the training of the lads who aren’t in the team is so important, the lifestyle, the commitment to the job, the commitment to the team.

"Don’t be the one that’s caught out partying or eating junk food because you’re not letting yourself down, you’re letting your teammates down. But I don’t think we need to worry about any of that in this group."

#1836. Spurs transfer news: Can Mikey Moore be recalled from FC Koln in January?

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:07

Tottenham Hotspur allegedly do not have the option to recall Mikey Moore from his loan at FC Koln.

Spurs' 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday afternoon has moved the club into ninth place in the Premier League table.

With a squad possessing depth and a schedule that lacks European football, Roberto De Zerbi is not exactly in desperate need of additions during the winter transfer window.

Nevertheless, academy graduate Moore is earning regular football in Germany, seemingly putting him in the thoughts of the Italian.

However, as per talkSPORT, Spurs may have to wait until the summer to reintegrate the winger.

Moore made the headlines on Friday courtesy of scoring for FC Koln against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga.

The 19-year-old's early effort at the Allianz Arena helped earn his side a 1-1 draw against the champions.

That goal was Moore's first in six starts and three substitute outings in Germany's top flight.

Nevertheless, Spurs are seemingly not in the position to automatically recall Moore should they wish to do so.

With Moore having already represented Spurs this season, he can only play for his parent club or Koln for the remainder of the campaign.

If Spurs earn a return to European football for 2027-28, Moore's homegrown status means that he will likely be used in De Zerbi's squad.

For now, though, it makes sense that he is playing a key role for Koln, who sit in 13th place in the Bundesliga table.

Should he continue to accumulate regular minutes, it will stand him in good stead for next season.

#1835. Macdonald: I was told my job was ‘bomb-proof’ – but eight days later Eastbourne Town sacked me

Macdonald’s four-and-a-half year run as manager of Town ended after Saturday’s 1-1 draw at home to Whitstable when he was sacked in a move that has angered many of the club’s fans and seen a number of players and support staff leave the club too.

He has spoken to Sussexworld and the Eastbourne Herald about the decision – and outlined some of the difficulties they had faced with injury and unavailability this season in a run of results that ironically had recently looked like it might be coming to an end.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Town confirmed Macdonald’s departure on Saturday in a statement and have since installed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager and asked fans to get behind him.

Macdonald said of his sacking: “It was a surprise to be honest and there was absolutely zero warning, which you often anticipate with this sort of thing.

"I spoke to the chairman eight days earlier (the day before the Sheppey game) and he told me on that call that my role was “bomb-proof” and that I had his backing.

"I had explained to him in the call how hard it had been this season, but we didn’t have a relationship where we talked regularly on the phone so we hadn’t had an opportunity to discuss things previously.

"On Saturday, the chairman told one of my assistants at the final whistle to tell me to come to the office. It was the first league game that the chairman had attended since August so I obviously didn’t think too much of it, but that was when he delivered the news to me around 20 minutes after the game had finished.

"He did it along with another member of staff who I’ve never been introduced to before, but is also apparently a committee member.

"The chairman told me my position was being ended at the club and said that they thought it would be better to announce it as a resignation, which I rejected.

"I wasn’t given a reason, despite asking for one multiple times. The chairman just kept shrugging and it wasn’t his fault it was just what the board wanted. I was told that the board held a vote on the previous Monday (November 16) and the decision was made, which is when they made a call to another manager on speaker to offer the job/sound out his interest. The likely new manager told me this on Saturday evening.

"The club then let me manage the Lewes game on the Tuesday, take training Thursday, sign two players on Friday and manage Saturday’s game without anybody saying anything to me, despite knowing they were going to sack me after the Saturday game."

It is Macdonald and one of his right-hand men, Ben Davis, who have been sacked. Macdonald said: “The club wanted my other two assistants, Matthew Elphick and Adam Davidson, to remain in position, but they have rejected that opportunity.”

Macdonald outlined some of the difficulties Town have faced this season which have left them struggling, having won just two league games to sit second from bottom of the Isthmian SE table after 19 games.

He told us: “It has been no secret that we have been completely decimated by injuries through the season and have only once played the same XI two games running. We had started to get bodies in the door and back on the pitch.

"We’d drawn our last two games and arguably could have won both, so it is frustrating that the club made the call they did when the tide was clearly turning.”

Macdonald outlined the injuries the squad had faced: Oliver Davies - ruptured PCL; Anesu Sismayi - Head injury; Marcin Ruda - fractured foot; JJ Walker - hip flexor & suspension; Leon Greig - knee injury (3 months missed); Luke Emberson - shin splints & groin; Aussie Pugh - ankle & knee; Aaron Capon - hamstring & back; Jack Murphy - heel & suspension; Sonny Walsh - jaw; Eliot Jenks - hamstring; Oli Deda - concussion (missed 3 games); Reuel Powell-Downey - hamstring; Arron Hopkinson - suspension.

He added: “That is a fraction of the list.”

Looking back at his time as Town boss, Macdonald talked about some of those who had helped him and his staff: “Since we’ve been at the club, David Jenkins has been absolutely incredible. The work he does for the club, the selflessness and support he gives it is truly unbelievable. He is what non-league is about. Anything we needed, he always did his best to help us with.

"Ross Perrin this season has also been a huge help to us and supported us throughout, as have Luci Del-Gaudio and Paul Lewis. Josh Claxton and Ed have both been incredible. What Josh has done with the social media and all other online stuff is just amazing and he done so much for the club that never got noticed. Josh has also left the football club.

"Former 23s and 18s managers Shaun Lee, Giuseppe Lombardelli and Ryan Reid were always a huge help and incredibly supportive. There are dozens of others that have backed and supported us throughout our time like Ken Wilkins and Chris Prior. Truly great people.

"A huge thank you to all the players over the years. They have done so much for us and we really appreciate all their efforts.

"The biggest thank you is to our management team and support staff, who have just been incredible throughout our time together at the club. Ben Davis, Matt Elphick, Adam Davidson, David Winterton, Roman Glazier and Dom Crowhurst have all made my Saturdays so enjoyable. They’ve all worked so hard for the players and deserve huge credit.”

Macdonald is in no hurry to find a new non-league job: “I would expect to relax and have a break from it all to be honest. I will try to take in other games and training sessions with other managers wherever I can. I’m trying not to think too much about what comes next because you can’t predict anything in non-league.”

He added: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”

We have asked Eastbourne Town if anyone wishes to respond to any of Macdonald’s comments.

Moreira – Left calf flexor strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Left medial flexor injury, from October 25. 12. Tomori – Right medial flexor injury, from October 29. 13. Pavlovic – Renal colic, from November 4 to 17. 13 days out and missed 2 games.

Total: Five traumatic/other and eight muscular from 15 matches played (11 Serie A, 4 Europa League).

So, while things might have felt quite bleak at various moments when gazing into a packed treatment room, Amorim has actually had a bit more luck than his predecessor when it comes to physical issues. Now he must hope that continues, or even that he gets luckier still.

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:08

Slovan Bratislava will be looking to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they host Real Betis at Tehelne Pole Stadion on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues sit bottom of the league phase table with no points from four matches, while Betis occupy 11th place with nine points.

Slovan defeated Celje away from home in the second leg of their playoff-round tie to secure a place in the Champions League main phase, marking a historic achievement for the club.

However, the Slovakian side have found the step up in quality difficult to handle, losing all four of their matches, scoring just once and conceding 17 goals.

Yaya Toure's side began their campaign with a heavy 6-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain before suffering further losses against Stuttgart, Roma and LASK.

Balancing their domestic and European commitments has also proved challenging, with their continental struggles seemingly affecting their league form, as they sit second in the Slovakian top flight, seven points behind leaders DAC 1904 despite having played a game more.

Perhaps most frustrating for Toure is Slovan's poor home form, with the Sky Blues winless in their last five matches at Tehelne Pole Stadion, drawing three of those encounters.

Real Betis have made a solid start to their European campaign, collecting three wins from four matches while scoring eight goals and conceding six.

El Glorioso opened their campaign with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Lille, coming from behind to claim all three points.

They followed that up with another thrilling 3-2 win against Porto before beating Feyenoord 1-0 to secure back-to-back home victories.

Manuel Pellegrini's side suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in their previous Champions League outing, but they have an excellent opportunity to climb the table with a victory over Slovan.

The back four of Sandro Cruz, Svetozar Markovic, Kenan Bajric and Daiki Matsuoka are expected to retain their places, with Peter Pokorny operating at the base of midfield.

Artur Gajdos appeared to pick up an injury in the previous game and could be replaced by Alexej Maros, while Andraz Sporar is set to continue up front, with Roman Cerepaki a doubt due to a back problem.

Real Betis are likely to be without Dani Ceballos, who is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return to action before the start of December.

Fran Garcia and Hector Bellerin are expected to retain their places in defence, while Diego Llorente could come into the side in place of Marc Bartra.

Antony picked up a knock in the derby but he has travelled with the squad, and should retain his place alongside Isco and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, with Jose Antonio Morante currently sidelined through injury.

Leeds United star Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the type of player Arsenal “could do with”, according to former Gunners winger Theo Walcott.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has enjoyed a new lease of life at Elland Road and has been named in the last two England squads, collecting the most recent of his 15 caps in the 3-2 Nations League win over Spain.

Walcott, who spent the bulk of his playing career at the Emirates Stadium, believes Calvert-Lewin could suit his former employers.

He told talkSPORT: “I look at someone like Dominic Calvert-Lewin. I think he's been outstanding this year. He's the kind of number nine Arsenal could do with in this moment of time.

“I think he's (Viktor Gyokeres) suited for an old-school winger, not one of those inverted ones who delay the crosses.

“He wants to be in those areas, he wants to be that player to get on the end of things. I don't think he times his runs, because at times, he's not sure when the ball is going to come in, if it will come in.

“As well, the way he plays affects everyone. Arsenal are used to playing with a false nine, to then everyone changing their dynamic of playing. I think it really inhibits the way Arsenal play. And I do like [Kai] Havertz, but I do feel like there's a position up for grabs.”

Calvert-Lewin struggled for fitness and form in his final years at Everton, who could not get him tied down to a new contract.

He became a free agent at the end of the 2024/25 season and Leeds’ swoop for him was widely regarded as a risky one.

However, their decision to hand a deal to the England international has been well and truly vindicated.

#1824. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

Clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

Jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

Yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

Understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

Zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

Lammens saves from Harry Wilson’s shot from 10 yards after Rodon’s underlapping ran down the right caught Amass off guard.

Senne Lammens to the rescue! 🧤A great reaction save from the Belgian 👏🇧🇪 pic.twitter.com/GRau9yk02n

Thompson tackles Rodon as he tried to lengthen his stride down the right.

Oddly Bornauw, who is poised to join Hamburg on loan, is the only player kept on from the first half for Leeds.

Gnonto, who is playing at right wing-back, is palyed down the line by Rodon and bends over a low cross looking for Calvert-Lewin’s late run. Lammens dives out to smother it.

Manchester United make three changes – Tynan Thompson, Toby Collyer and Dan Armer replace Santos, Heaven and Dorgu.

Cairns; Rodon, Bornauw, Cresswell; Justin, Ampadu, Stach, Gnonto; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

On this evidence he might be worth a punt for goals and assists topping 25 this season like they did in 2024-25 for Brentford. Though he may have to take pens off Bruno Fernandes to get there.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

Yoro hooks Bogle’s long chip out for a throw-in. This time Leeds take it short and try to engineer a crossing opportunity but go back to Trafford when they can’t find space.

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (Aaronson) James robs Tyler Fletcher in the inside-left position and sprints towards the 18-yard line before slipping it inside to Aaronson. The once erratic finisher takes a touch to put Heaven on his heels then slots a right-foot shot crisply into the bottom left corner.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

Tanaka has two long throws in from the right. Dorgu heads the first one out for the second which is flicked on by Bornauw but Man Utd clear the second ball.

Tyler Fletcher takes a trick out of his old man’s book by grabbing James round the waist once the speed merchant had knocked the ball past him. Leeds go backwards from the free-kick as Man Utd’s press hounds them.

Trafford confidently catches the cross from the corner then bowls it out 40 yards to set Aaronson off on a counter. His solo raid down the right is stymied by Amass’s diligent defending.

Mbeumo drives down the gap between Muharemovic and Bijol, tries to find Doegu but Bornauw slides in to intercept but only succeeds in playing it back to Mbeumo who lashes a left-foot shot that Trafford tips round the right post at full stretch.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

There is certainly more urgency about Manchester United’s play. Leeds are living dangerously.

In the couple of minutes after the goal Manchester United almost punish Leeds’ high defensive line again but Muharemovic rides to the rescue. Bijol is a very good box defender but he lacks pace.

United’s start has been bright and confident and the system they playing is flipping between 4-4-2 and 4-2-3-1 and the first thought is always to go forward. The goal they have just scored is indicative of how they have started and it’s a positive for Joshua Zirkzee, who has spent much of his time at Old Trafford under a cloud, to have finished it with aplomb. Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 0 (Zirkzee) Leeds, on the attack, lose possession down the middle and Dorgu works it out to Mbeumo who beats Bijol 20 yards inside the Man Utd half. He pokes it through the Leeds captain;s legs and hares off down the wing until he gets to the 18 yard line and from there he bends the perfect pass to Zirkzee who sweeps home a shot into the bottom left with his left foot.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Manchester United build slowly down the right and then Dalot injects some urgency by whipping in a low cross. Zirkzee meets it not so much with a shot but with the timing of his arrival on the ball, deflecting it towards the right of goal powerfully, Trafford gets down well to save.

Leeds cross the free-kick into the box and James’ volley strikes a defender in the midriff and then hits the deck when going for the rebound, bundled over by Yoro. The ref waves play on and Manchester Unted counter with Amad Diallo dribbling down the right until tackled by Chadwick at the price of a corner.

Dorgu is penalised for a scissors-tackle on Bornauw. He did get the ball but only after he had caught he blond defender with his other leg. Carrick leaps up to protest, as does Farke but he is saying that Dorgu has twice slid in wildly.

Leeds defend the corner fairly solidly but Manchester United recover possession 30 yards out and set up Dalot to have a crack with a dipping, swerving effort that Trafford pats down in front of his face and catches after it bounces.

Amad Diallo finds Mbeumo down the right and he tries to head the ball across the box but Muharemovic is well-placed to head it back out but an attempt to nod the ball back to Trafford goes astray and the £45m man can’t stop it going out for a corner.

Leeds free-kick for either a foul by Amass on Aaronson or Dorgu on Bogle. Hard to tell, one was a split-second after the other.

Amass pulls back Bogle after being tackled by the Leeds wing-back and Leeds build up the right from the free-kick, earning themselves a throw-in parallel with the penalty spot. In Ampadu’s absence Tanaka is the trebuchet, hurling in the long throw that Bornauw nods on but Manchester united clear the second ball.

Leeds work the ball back to Taafford from the kick off and he chips it long up the right. Dorgu heads it out for a throw-in. Leeds go backwards again and pass the ball around confidently.

Jaka Bijol captains Leeds, Diogo Dalot leads out Manchester United.

They would be as well delaying the start of the game here the concourses outside this magnificent and historic stadium are packed with crowds taking in the solar eclipse. What a genuinely extraordinary moment! There will be plenty of time later this evening to talk about the football, for now attentions are firmly elsewhere!

🤩 Ready for a first #LUFC start! pic.twitter.com/KU5ica0HcG

And for Senne Lammens, a new shirt number, from 31 to Numero Uno:

Lammens is not the only one. Marcus Rashford wore 39 in his debut season with Man Utd, moved to 19 for the next three then changed to 10 when Zlatan Ibrahimovic left the club. The 10 shirt has been given to Matheus Cunha so now he will wear 14, the number he had at Barcelona in his Liga title-winning season.

If you’re watching in the UK, the match is live on ITV. A friendly! Live on ITV.  That’s Croke Park for you.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.
