#1786. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1785. Mauricio Pochettino seals Manchester United coup as ex-Arsenal man arrives

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Manchester United have hired former Arsenal coach Sam Wilson, who has already started work as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

Wilson left Arsenal in the summer, having been at the club for 12 years.

He was the lead physical performance coach under Mikel Arteta up until the end of last season, playing his part in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning season.

Wilson left the Gunners as part of the club’s overhaul of their medical department, with significant changes made in an attempt to address the injury problems that have hindered the squad in recent seasons.

After departing his role at Arsenal, Wilson briefly joined Parma, where he was appointed head of performance by Arteta’s former assistant Carlos Cuesta.

However, Cuesta was sacked in September and Wilson left the club a month later. He has now made a swift return to England.

Wilson was on the bench at Anfield on Sunday as Pochettino took charge of United for the first time.

He has joined United as a first-team fitness coach and will play his part in what is expected to be a key focus of Pochettino’s reign.

United rank second-last in the running stats in the Premier League this season, in stark contrast to the stats recorded by Pochettino’s teams at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

During his time at Arsenal, Wilson oversaw a lot of the individual training work with players returning from injury issues.

When Bukayo Saka came back from injury to face Fulham last year and scored within seven minutes, he ran straight to Wilson on the bench to celebrate with him.

#1784. Peter Schmeichel sets ‘target’ for Man Utd after Liverpool thrashing

Peter Schmeichel believes simply avoiding relegation should be Mauricio Pochettino’s main ‘target’ at Manchester United this season.

Pochettino took charge of United for the first time away to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon and it proved a nightmare start for the Argentine, with his side thumped 4-0 at Anfield.

The Red Devils were reduced to ten men in only the tenth minute after Leny Yoro brought down Alexander Isak, and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Dominik Szoboszlai scored with the resulting free-kick.

Man-of-the-match Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the hosts out of sight.

The result ensured United remained firmly in the relegation zone at the end of the weekend’s drama, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The Old Trafford giants, who now lead Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions), will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters at Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

‘Realistically, can Manchester United just finish tenth or 12th? It would be okay,’ former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said on Viaplay following the side’s heavy defeat on Merseyside.

‘I know it’s silly to say but we are in the relegation zone and this team looks like a team that could get relegated.

It was some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro that led to Liverpool’s breakthrough against United, with the latter guilty of fouling Alexander Isak after failing to cover his centre-back partner.

And while it was De Ligt that made the initial mistake, Yoro was the main focus of Schmeichel’s post-match criticism.

‘I think Isak is doing really well,’ the Dane said when watching back replays of the move.

‘When Yoro comes in, Isak cuts across him and yes, he brings him down.

‘It’s terrible defending, it is. Not for that on its own but why is he not reading the ball over the top, over De Ligt?

‘Yoro should have been supporting his co-defender and he’s not.’

Schmeichel has long been an outspoken critic of Lisandro Martinez and branded the defender ‘disgraceful’ in the wake of United’s 2-0 loss to Chelsea last month.

It came just a fortnight after Martinez had launched an explosive attack on United’s board, in which he suggested the squad had been repeatedly let down by the club’s recruitment team.

‘I’m fed up talking about him. Honestly, I’m fed up talking about him,’ Schmeichel said of Martinez following United’s latest setback.

‘He’s a guy that criticises people upstairs, criticises his team-mates… I think you have to perform better than that, I really do think that.

‘You can through not all of the goals, but you can go through a couple of the goals and he’s there, at the centre of that, and he could have done something to at least make it harder for Liverpool to score.’

Mauricio Pochettino may have left Gary Neville ‘absolutely stunned’ by picking Matthijs de Ligt against Liverpool, but the Manchester United manger says there was a simple reason for it.

The new Red Devils boss had a tough opening game in charge as he took his side to Anfield and it ended up being a nightmare debut for the Argentine.

Leny Yoro was shown a red card after eight minutes and Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick.

Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz also netted to complete a comfortable 4-0 win for Andoni Iraola’s men.

The 27-year-old looked a long way off Premier League pace as he was run ragged by the Liverpool front line.

Asked why he went for De Ligt alongside Yoro over Harry Maguire, who started on the bench but has been playing regularly this season, Pochettino said: ‘He was training, he played in Champions League before the international duty. I think, when we arrived we saw the combination.’

#1782. Did ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe really need eye surgery after staring at solar eclipse?

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour quickly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

#1781. San Jose Earthquakes vs Houston Dynamo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 22 Nov 2026 16:28

Featuring in the playoffs for the first time since 2023, the San Jose Earthquakes will welcome the Houston Dynamo to PayPal Park on Tuesday for game one of that best-of-three series.

A 3-1 loss at Minnesota United on Decision Day meant the Quakes finished fourth in the MLS table out West, while Houston was a point behind them in fifth after a 1-0 home defeat to St Louis City.

After narrowly missing the post-season a year ago, San Jose got the job done this time around, earning 52 points, 11 more than they had in 2025.

Bruce Arena guided them to a 14-win regular season in 2026, the most for this club since 2013, when they also won 14 times.

Heading into the post-season, San Jose are on a six-match MLS unbeaten run at home, winning their last match at PayPal Park 2-1 versus Real Salt Lake on Halloween.

This year they have found the back of the net in all but two MLS affairs at home, while scoring multiple goals on nine occasions.

On Tuesday they can claim their first playoff victory since 2012 and earn their first post-season triumph at home since 2004 (2-0 over the Kansas City Wizards).

The Quakes are unbeaten in their last four MLS games against Houston, blanking them 1-0 at PayPal Park earlier this season.

After failing to make the playoffs for the first time in his tenure last year, Ben Olsen and the Dynamo bounced back with a much more consistent 2026 campaign.

During this regular season, Houston collected 51 points, 14 more than a year ago, while finishing seven places higher in the Western Conference table.

Their 43 goals scored during the regular season were the fewest among the MLS sides that made the playoffs, though they gave up the third fewest in the West (43) as well.

A win in game one would mark the first for this club away from home in the post-season since 2017, when they defeated the Timbers 2-1 in Portland.

In 2026, the Dynamo created the third-fewest big chances in MLS (66) and conceded the fourth-fewest goals per match (1.3).

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

San Jose will be missing DeJuan Jones as he recovers from Achilles tendon surgery, while Nonso Adimabua may not be ready to return from his lower body injury.

Preston Judd had their only strike against Minnesota the last time out, with Angus Gunn conceding three second-half goals between the sticks as he drew back into the fold over Earl Edwards Jr.

Over at Houston, Marcelo Saracchi may not be available due to a knock, and Jimmy Maurer is doubtful because of a head injury.

Guilherme will be relied upon to provide scoring for this team in the playoffs, with the Brazilian leading them with 16 goals in the regular season, along with 10 assists, while Mateusz Bogusz was second with eight goals.

San Jose Earthquakes possible starting lineup:

Gunn; Kikanovic, Munie, Romney, Ricketts; Vieira, Lowen; Harkes, Tsakiris, Werner; Judd

Bond; Ennali, Andrade, Resch, Halter, Negri; Herrera, Artur, Bogusz; Foster, Guilherme

The Quakes play with much more aggression and on the front foot at home, and we believe they have enough creativity to find a way through a strong Dynamo backline that could be defending for long stretches in game one.

#1780. ‘Wake up!’: Gary Neville slaps himself in the face TWICE during Manchester United rant

Manchester United’s heavy defeat by Liverpool led to Gary Neville slapping himself in the face twice on live television as he took aim at their dreadful defending.

Mauricio Pochettino’s debut as Man Utd boss ended in a 4-0 loss at Anfield, with the Red Devils collapsing after Leny Yoro’s early red card.

Again criticising United’s defence, Neville called out the players’ body language, accusing them of being asleep.

He said on Sky Sports: “I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here,” before pointing to his head.

“I never see any of them look like that. They look like that,” Neville added, providing a gormless look and pausing for several seconds, before stating “wake up” and slapping himself in the face twice.

With fellow pundit Jamie Carragher bursting into uncontrollable laughter, Neville finished his impassioned rant by adding: “You play for Man United!”

Roy Keane also fumed over United’s latest capitulation and called out Neville for initially suggesting that things could have been worse after Yoro’s early dismissal.

He said: “If I hear that one more time from the lads on commentary saying 4-0 is not too bad and the team were down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done.

“I thought United were desperate, I thought they were so bad, and Neville who has played for United hundreds of times said he’s okay with four nil? Obviously it [the red card] doesn’t help.

“But are you telling me they couldn’t have done better? At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality.

#1779. Manchester United players will need a slap if they agree with Gary Neville relegation prediction

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

#1778. Chelsea get new Morgan Rogers penalty review after Leeds handball controversy

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

VAR was correct not to overrule Michael Oliver after he awarded a controversial penalty against Morgan Rogers for handball against Leeds, per Dermot Gallagher.

The match was level at 1-1 when Rogers attempted to block a shot from Jayden Bogle. He turned his back in doing so and the ball appeared to catch him on his upper arm, with Oliver immediately pointing to the spot.

VAR reviewed the incident and allowed the penalty to stand, which Dominic Calvert-Lewin duly buried to put Leeds 2-1 up. The match ended 4-1 in the visitors’ favour.

Chelsea fans were left confused by the decision, with many suspecting the ball had caught Rogers above his sleeve and thus did not warrant handball. Rogers, meanwhile, appeared to protest that the ball had hit him in the face.

Xabi Alonso was similarly unimpressed with the decision, saying post-match: “I don’t agree. I think that it was harsh from Michael Oliver. For me it was not a penalty.”

But, speaking on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch, former Premier League referee Gallagher has opined that VAR was correct to allow Oliver’s decision to stand, pointing out that there was not sufficient evidence to overturn it.

The VAR reviewed a number of different angles of the incident, but none conclusively absolved Rogers.

“You can watch replays, you can watch a multitude of angles, some will say it hit (Rogers) on the elbow and some say the face,” said Gallagher. “There is no conclusive evidence to say the referee is wrong, so he has to give a penalty.

“We are not trying to prove the referee wrong. He gave a penalty. What I am saying is there is no evidence to say the referee is wrong, not that the VAR is gonna say ‘this is the right decision’.

“The referee has given the decision, and the evidence says the referee is not wrong.”

Jay Bothroyd concurred, admitting he felt that the ball might have hit Rogers too high, but that he would not have liked to see the penalty overturned.

“You have got to stick with the referee's decision,” he declared. “It looked like it hit his sleeve but they have a camera to show the elbow. It is difficult to see.

“When you look at that, (everyone has) an opinion), so you have to stick with the referee's decision.

#1773. Serie A striker linked as Harry Kane replacement for Bayern with PSG lurking

By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 17:04

Bayern Munich have been linked with Roma striker Donyell Malen after Harry Kane suffered a long-term ankle injury, with Paris Saint-Germain also reportedly keen. Kane, 33, will be out for several months, a blow that could push Bayern to sign a goalscorer in the January transfer window.

Kane was injured on Friday night in the 1-1 draw with Cologne on the 10th Bundesliga matchday, and he has suffered a torn syndesmotic ligament. He must undergo surgery and will miss several months of competition. It is a major blow for boss Vincent Kompany, who has no other specialist number nine with the same status in his squad.

Given the fixtures ahead, the Champions League above all, the Bundesliga giants could use the winter window to act. Top Mercato reported that the injury could make Marseille fear a Bayern move for Amine Gouiri, but he is not the only forward who could interest the Allianz Arena club.

According to Calciomercato, Bayern are expected to position themselves for Malen, the prolific Netherlands striker. The Italian outlet says the 27-year-old ‘deserves the attention’ of the Bavarian hierarchy. Bayern have not made an offer, and signing him in the coming weeks looks very complicated given his outstanding 2026-27 season with Roma.

Malen has scored 16 goals in 15 matches in all competitions. The former Borussia Dortmund player leads the Serie A scoring charts with 12 goals in 11 appearances. On Saturday he scored four goals in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. His xG of 9.71, higher than Kane’s, confirms that the number 14 is overperforming.

The statistics may impress several clubs more prestigious than Roma, but Bayern have no chance of convincing the Italian club to release their number one attacking weapon in the middle of the season. Malen is under contract until June 2030, with a market value of £47m, and will not be sold before the summer of 2027.

That should also cool PSG’s interest. Faced with injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the French capital club could see boss Luis Enrique ‘ask president Al-Khelaifi to return to the market, and asking for a top-level player like Malen is not heresy’, according to the report. Like Bayern, however, PSG will almost certainly meet a categorical refusal from Roma, at least in January.

#1771. Three stats show why Manchester United should be VERY worried about relegation

Mauricio Pochettino has already admitted that new employers Manchester United are in a relegation battle - with some key trends and statistics highlighting why the Red Devils should be genuinely worried about the drop.

Man Utd offered little resistance on Pochettino’s managerial debut at Anfield on Sunday as they were ripped apart 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool following the early dismissal of Leny Yoro.

Fans will have seen that during their own season of constant struggle last term, Tottenham already had 18 points on the board at this stage of the campaign - 10 more than United’s current tally.

Spurs only confirmed their Premier League survival on the final day, edging out rivals West Ham by a single point in a hugely dramatic finish.

There are more alarming numbers and patterns from Premier League history that do not bode well for free-falling United’s fortunes this season.

Over the past 20 years, at least one team in the bottom three after 11 games has gone on to be relegated by the end of the season.

In total, 56.66 per cent of clubs in the relegation zone after 11 matches have finished there.

Pochettino’s side will take solace in the fact that seven teams have previously beaten the drop after picking up exactly eight points from their opening 11 fixtures.

But that doesn’t tell the full story. Teams with only eight points and sitting in the relegation zone after 11 games have survived on just two previous occasions, with six dropping down to the Championship.

Only Newcastle in 2006/07 and Southampton in 2019/20 beat the drop after starting off with eight points from their first 11 games to languish in the bottom three.

Ipswich sat outside the relegation zone in 2023/24 with eight points from 11 matches, but were unable to stay up come May.

‘Wake up!’: Neville slaps himself in the face TWICE during Man Utd rant

Pochettino seals Man Utd coup as ex-Arsenal man arrives

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Over the last 20 years, 31 teams with eight points or fewer from their opening 11 fixtures failed to survive; only 24 sides stayed up with that starting tally.

In more concern for United, the other two teams currently in the relegation zone make up six of those latter examples.

Crystal Palace are used to starting slow - twice they have begun the season with four points from 11 games, only to record 11th-place finishes on both occasions.

In total, the Eagles have recovered from eight points or fewer after 11 games to stave off relegation four times, while Sunderland have achieved that feat twice.

What does United’s own history tell us about the current side’s chances of beating the drop?

When United were last relegated from the top-flight, all the way back in 1973/74, the Red Devils had a higher points total after 11 games.

Under the current rules for three points for a win, rather than the two awarded at that time, Tommy Docherty’s side would have had 11 points from their first 11 matches of the 1973/74 First Division season.

In reality they had just nine, after three wins and two draws. Goalkeeper Alex Stepney was their joint-top goalscorer after converting two penalties.

United finished the season 21st out of 22 teams, five points from safety. Perhaps United fans will take solace from the fact that this season’s start more closely resembles the beginning of the campaign prior to that relegation - five draws, one win and six losses from 12 games.

In 1972/73, United managed to salvage an 18th-place finish in the old First Division, comfortably beating the drop. Of course, the next season they were relegated for the first time since 1938.

#1769. Manchester United make Leny Yoro red card appeal decision after Liverpool rout

Manchester United have notified the Football Association (FA) that they intend to appeal Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Man Utd boss at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool then romped to an easy 4-0 win, with Pochettino afterwards lamenting referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro as “unfair”.

The Argentine believed that his player did not deny a goalscoring opportunity, meaning that he should not have seen red.

Yoro clipped the heels of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool attacker bore down on goal, but Pochettino and United fans felt that goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the loose ball before Isak, negating the goalscoring potential.

Under current FA rules, clubs have 14 days to submit an appeal, with United back in action on Saturday as they host Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford.

With his current three-game domestic suspension, Yoro would also miss the trip to Newcastle and visit of Coventry early next month, but remain available for Champions League meetings with Sporting and RB Leipzig.

Yoro’s dismissal on Merseyside was his second in two months, having also received his marching orders in a Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid in October.

Former United boss Michael Carrick questioned that decision at the time and stated his belief that it was not a red card, but no appeal was made by the club.

#1767. Longo: Rabiot renewal, Endrick, Inacio and more – key topics during Friday’s summit

Gerry Cardinale had a meeting with the AC Milan management at Casa Milan yesterday, during which there were four key topics, according to reports.

Cardinale has arrived in the city in good time for Milan’s game against Frosinone tomorrow. Yesterday, there was a summit with the Milan management, including the CEO Massimo Calvelli, Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner, and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão.

This was reported by Sky Italia (via MilanEye) and various outlets, highlighting how Cardinale wants to be ready for the January window and even the summer window. Markus Krösche will be there to help him with that, set to be announced next week, as Gazzetta dello Sport reported.

#1766. Feyenoord vs Porto - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 22 Nov 2026 18:17

Feyenoord will be desperate to end a six-match winless run when they welcome Porto to De Kuip for Tuesday's Champions League league-phase encounter.

Both sides have collected just three points from their opening four European fixtures, leaving the Portuguese visitors 26th in the 36-team table and their Dutch hosts languishing in 32nd.

Feyenoord head into Tuesday's encounter after suffering three consecutive defeats, the latest of which came at De Kuip on Saturday when they were beaten 3-2 by Excelsior, who secured their first league victory at the ground in 46 years.

The hosts made a bright start by taking the lead through Givairo Read barely two minutes into the contest, but three goals in succession left Jan Plug's own goal little more than a consolation as De Stadionclub slipped to fifth in the Eredivisie table.

More concerning for Giovanni van Bronckhorst is his side's defensive record, having conceded at least three goals in each of their last three outings across all competitions, with Saturday's setback following a 5-3 defeat at Heerenveen and a 3-0 home loss to Inter Milan on matchday four of the Champions League league phase.

That continental defeat was the 10th in Feyenoord's last 13 European matches, while it also extended an unwanted run that has seen them concede the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings, including defeats to Barcelona and Real Betis as well as their victory over Como on matchday two.

With the prospect of another early European exit looming, the Dutch club know that another setback on Tuesday would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout rounds hanging by a thread, having already fallen short in last season's Europa League league phase, where they finished 29th.

However, the hosts face a difficult examination against a Porto side who finally got their Champions League campaign up and running with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Napoli at the Estadio do Dragao on matchday four.

Francesco Farioli's men had suffered defeats to Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV in their opening three league-phase fixtures, but goals from Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion inspired a convincing response against the Italian outfit.

That being said, Porto have won each of their opening 11 league matches this term to establish a five-point gap atop the Primeira Liga table, though the Dragons were made to work harder in Friday's Taca de Portugal encounter with third-tier Paredes, eventually progressing on penalties after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes.

Back on the continental stage, the Dragons, featuring in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years, will continue their quest to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance, having progressed to the last 16 in their previous two campaigns.

Nevertheless, the visitors have not always enjoyed travelling to the Netherlands, failing to win any of their last four away matches against Dutch opposition (D2, L2), including  both previous visits to Feyenoord, having drawn at De Kuip in the Champions League in 1993 before suffering a 2-0 defeat there in 2019, while both of Porto’s victories in this fixture have come on home soil.

Feyenoord are monitoring the fitness of Anis Hadj Moussa, who returned from international duty with an ankle injury and missed Saturday's defeat to Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also doubtful after being withdrawn at half time against Excelsior, with Van Bronckhorst indicating that the defender was struggling with a foot problem, while Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain sidelined with injuries.

Thomas Beelen (leg), Jordan Bos (ACL) and Jerry St. Juste (shin) are expected to remain unavailable, leaving the hosts with limited defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for Feyenoord at the weekend, although Luciano Valente could be preferred on the left flank of attack against Porto.

As for the visitors, long-term absentee Vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a leg injury, while William Gomes has recovered from an ankle injury and returned to full training, although his involvement on Tuesday remains uncertain.

Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is also dealing with a right knee problem and is ineligible to feature, having not been included in Porto's Champions League league-phase squad.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang will face his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord over the summer, while on-loan striker Santiago Gimenez returns to the Netherlands after representing the Dutch side between 2022 and 2025.

Ernst; Read, Kraaijeveld, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Valente, Hadj Moussa; Ferri

Diogo Costa; Alberto Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Zaidu; Veiga, Rosario, Froholdt; Pepe, Sainz, Andre Silva

Feyenoord's six-match winless run and continued defensive problems make it difficult to back the hosts, particularly against a Porto side who showed what they are capable of with their emphatic victory over Napoli.

The Portuguese visitors have also enjoyed the better of this fixture historically, and we expect them to take advantage of the host’s current struggles to secure their first away victory at De Kuip.

#1765. Kobbie Mainoo issues stark Manchester United relegation warning: ‘No one is coming to save us’

Kobbie Mainoo has warned Manchester United that there is “no one coming to save us” after defeat by Liverpool left the club mired in the relegation zone.

The Red Devils found themselves on the back foot almost immediately at Anfield as Leny Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute for taking out Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resultant free kick and United never recovered, going on to lose 4-0.

It was a wretched start to Mauricio Pochettino’s time as the club’s manager. His debut is the worst since Lal Hilditch lost by the same margin to Bolton in 1926.

READ MORE: The three stats that show Man Utd should be VERY worried about relegation

United were already in the drop zone as they headed to Anfield, but have slipped from 18th to 19th with this defeat, having taken eight points from their first 11 matches. They are one of two clubs in England’s top four divisions to have won only one match this season.

Academy product Mainoo is fully aware of the club’s peril, and has issued a stark warning to his team-mates that they must take initiative if they are to dodge the drop.

“It’s all about character now,” he told MUTV.

“We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been and no one is coming to save us.

“There’s no helping hands coming, so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working and hopefully it’ll come good.”

Pochettino will hope to pick up a first win as United boss when they visit Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, but he will be all too aware of the tricky run of Premier League fixtures he has waiting for him back in England. United host Brentford next, before visiting Newcastle.

Mainoo continued: “(Anfield) is a tough place to come, but I can’t fault the boys on their fight. We have to take the pain from the game and move on with it.

“The games are still coming thick and fast, so we don’t have time to dwell on it.

“We’re all committed. No one is going anywhere and we’re all leaning on each other.

“We all know what we have to do and we all know with the new manager, we need to get behind him, keep working in training. That’s all we can do.”

#1763. Arsenal handed David Raya injury boost as Mikel Arteta reveals huge new update

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that David Raya‘s shoulder injury is “not too serious”, but he will miss Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund.

The influential Gunners goalkeeper came off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday evening.

Raya’s late collision with Magpies striker William Osula did not initially appear to be a serious one but it was enough for the Spaniard to be rendered unable to continue and he looked in considerable pain as he walked off the pitch.

He was sent for scans on Sunday in order to learn the severity of the injury and Raya then took no part in Arsenal’s open training session on Monday morning.

Deputies Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier were out on the pitch without their team-mate at London Colney and the pair now look set to battle it out to start against Dortmund on Tuesday night, with Kepa having replaced Raya for the closing stages at St James’ Park.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Monday afternoon, Arteta confirmed that it was indeed a shoulder injury for Raya, who was pictured wearing a sling on his left arm on social media on Sunday while out in London.

“He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious,” Arteta said. “We need some more tests tomorrow but it’s quite encouraging.

“With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

“The doctor explained but it’s quite technical. When you look at the action, it doesn’t seem to be much. The extent of the pain that he had and how much he was struggling, it was quite worrying.”

He added: “We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at the moment. The first tests that we have done showed something that is much more encouraging.

“Tomorrow we need to reaffirm that to be able to give you some more specific information.

“There was no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would have have ruled him out for months. Let’s see.”

With the last international break of 2026 having already taken place, club football will continue relentlessly for the next few months and Raya’s injury has come at an inopportune time for Arsenal.

Arteta’s side face big Champions League matches against Dortmund and Real Madrid in the next couple of weeks, as well as Premier League games against rivals Manchester City and Tottenham.

#1762. Liverpool 4-0 Man United: Highlights, man of the match, stats as Mauricio Pochettino's 10 men mauled

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 18:23, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 18:32

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United tenure began in nightmarish fashion as Liverpool tore the 10-man Red Devils to shreds in a 4-0 Premier League rout at Anfield.

Any hope of a customary new manager bounce was wiped out within just eight minutes for Man United, as Pochettino's first controversial selection call backfired horribly.

A defensive blunder from Matthijs de Ligt - making his first Premier League start since November 2025 - preceded Leny Yoro being sent off, Dominik Szoboszlai firing in the resulting free kick, and Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool's lead all within the space of five minutes.

Pochettino responded by introducing Harry Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo and switching to a back five, which succeeded in shoring up the Man United defence, but only for so long.

Liverpool's inevitable third belatedly arrived via Rio Ngumoha in the 66th minute, before substitute Victor Munoz capped off a four-midable display from the Merseyside giants.

The Reds have leapfrogged Bournemouth into fourth place in the Premier League table and are just one point shy of Brighton & Hove Albion and Manchester City, while Man Utd remain 19th, one point adrift of safety.

Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann told Sports Mole before the game that Liverpool were the favourites to beat Man United, even if Iraola's men were facing the Red Devils at an inopportune time.

However, the scoreline in the top left-hand corner would suggest that Liverpool hosted Man United at the most opportune time, as Pochettino's delayed arrival, lack of preparation time and eyebrow-raising defensive decisions ultimately spelled disaster.

Some may have questioned why De Ligt had been starved of minutes so far this season, but a complete absence of defensive awareness from the Dutchman displayed exactly why, and that solitary moment killed Man Utd's hopes of a shock success early doors.

The visitors still kept the Reds at bay for longer than expected after going 2-0 down, leading to a hint of frustration from the Anfield faithful, but Iraola's men were perpetually comfortable and soon displayed the ruthless edge their numerical advantage demanded.

In contrast, the Red Devils have now conceded more goals than any other team in Europe's big five leagues this season, and while it is hard to draw too many conclusions from Pochettino's debut - given his side were down a man since the eighth minute - the words 'relegation' and 'Man United' may soon be used in the same sentence unironically.

Amid the Mancunian misery, however, Liverpool and their burgeoning attack enhanced their Champions League credentials to the maximum, while potentially reigniting hope of a sensational title surge.

#1760. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

#1759. Mauricio Pochettino makes key change from Michael Carrick era as Manchester United bid to dodge the drop

Mauricio Pochettino has already instituted a major change at Manchester United in a bid to lift the club’s standards and dodge relegation.

The Argentine’s United tenure got off to a grim start at Anfield on Sunday as Leny Yoro was shown an early red card and Liverpool went on to bag four goals.

The result leaves the club 19th in the Premier League, with the prospect of relegation - or, at the very least, being involved in the relegation battle - more real than ever.

But as Pochettino discovers the true scale of the task at hand, he has wasted little time in imposing his methods on United.

That has begun with scrapping a rule imposed by his predecessor Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the November international break.

While in the job, Carrick had habitually handed the United squad a day off following a match, but Pochettino has promptly done away with that provision.

His players reported to Carrington bright and early on Monday morning for recovery sessions, with a Champions League meeting with Sporting looming on Wednesday evening.

Pochettino has pushed forward their arrival time, too, with some players touching down at the training ground as early as 8.30am.

It has been a busy few days at Carrington. Pochettino has hired a new strength and conditioning coach to help accommodate his focus on high-pressing football, while the club are also appealing Yoro’s red card.

They are doing so on the basis that Senne Lammens looked set to beat Alexander Isak in his footrace, and, thus, Yoro’s clumsy tackle did not constitute denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Reacting to the penalty decision post-match, Pochettino said: “It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after [eight] minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

"In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”

#1758. Liverpool 4-0 Man United: How "electric" Rio Ngumoha gave Andoni Iraola the big Anfield win he needed

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 18:40

Written by David Lynch, Liverpool expert:

If Andoni Iraola had been allowed to write the script for this game, it would probably have played out in broadly similar fashion.

Liverpool came into their latest clash with bitter rivals Manchester United having enjoyed a healthy start under the Basque, yet with a few question marks still over them.

That is exactly why this victory was extra sweet for Iraola, because his team answered each of them across the course of an enjoyable afternoon at Anfield.

The first concerned a poor home record that had seen the Reds take just five points from a possible 15, and which was clearly enhanced here.

The second related to their record in big games thanks to recent defeats to Manchester City and Arsenal.

Yes, United are in a tricky spot at the moment, but it can never be said that a meeting between England's two biggest clubs is not 'big'.

The third, meanwhile, was about whether Liverpool had shown enough in terms of free-flowing football, and they surely answered that in tearing the Red Devils apart here, largely through the electric Rio Ngumoha.

Clearly, it would be remiss not to mention Leny Yoro's early sending off as a decisive moment in the contest and the hosts' bid to tick certain boxes.

But judgement of Liverpool's issues this term has hardly been dripping in nuance, with key refereeing decisions against both City and Arsenal ignored, for example.

As such, it is surely only fair to take this result and performance at face value, as Iraola and his players likely will.

That means they will come away from this afternoon feeling like they are a team building momentum under a new manager, which is exactly what they are.
