#1757. Prediction: Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United

Manchester United turn their attention back to the Champions League on Wednesday night when they travel to the Estadio Jose Alvalade to face Sporting Lisbon.

The visitors arrive in Portugal reeling from another damaging Premier League defeat, while Sporting are in a much healthier position as they continue their pursuit of a place in the Champions League knockout rounds. At the halfway stage of the league phase, Sporting sit 10th in the 36-team standings, seven places and three points above United.

Sporting have made a solid start to their Champions League campaign and remain firmly in the hunt for automatic qualification.

The Portuguese side have taken nine points from their opening four league-phase matches, recording victories over Galatasaray, Lens and Shakhtar Donetsk. Their only setback came in a disappointing 3-2 home defeat against LASK Linz on matchday three.

Their most recent European outing saw them edge past Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, and Sporting now head into this fixture under the guidance of new head coach Paulo Fonseca, who has enjoyed a positive start since replacing Rui Borges earlier this month. Sporting have won both matches under his leadership so far.

Before the international break, the Lions claimed a narrow 1-0 Primeira Liga victory over Moreirense, before a heavily rotated side eased to a 4-0 win over fourth-tier Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal on Saturday. Despite those positive results, Sporting remain nine points behind league leaders Porto domestically.

One statistic will particularly encourage the hosts ahead of Wednesday’s clash. Sporting have scored in each of their last 22 Champions League group-stage or league-phase matches, the longest such run by a Portuguese club.

Sporting are hopeful of welcoming back Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos, both of whom are recovering from muscle injuries, although their involvement remains uncertain.

Fonseca is expected to restore several key players to the starting lineup, including Goncalo Inacio, Ivan Fresneda, Issa Doumbia, Rodrigo Zalazar and Geny Catamo. Chelsea loanee Jesse Derry is also pushing for a place in the side.

Colombian striker Luis Suarez is expected to return after being rested at the weekend. He has scored 13 goals in 15 appearances this season, including four in four Champions League matches.

Manchester United make the trip to Portugal searching for a response after a disastrous start to the Mauricio Pochettino era.

The Argentine watched his side suffer a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with United reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro’s controversial early red card. The defeat left the Red Devils 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points, their lowest tally after 11 matches since the 1972-73 season.

Pochettino has publicly acknowledged that the club is involved in a relegation battle and now faces the challenge of tightening a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season, more than any other club in Europe’s top five leagues.

European form has been inconsistent for United. They have beaten Sabah and Roma but suffered defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. The victory over Roma was particularly dramatic, with the Red Devils coming back from two goals down to win 3-2.

United’s away record in the Champions League offers little encouragement. They have won only one of their last 11 away matches in the competition, a 2-0 victory at Villarreal in 2021-22.

There is at least some comfort in the head-to-head record. United have won three of their previous four meetings with Sporting, including both group-stage clashes during their successful 2007-08 Champions League campaign.

United remain without injured trio Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko. There are also doubts over Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and reserve goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The visitors will definitely be without Matheus Cunha, who is suspended after being sent off in the previous Champions League fixture despite scoring the winning goals against Roma.

Matthijs de Ligt endured a difficult outing against Liverpool and could make way for Harry Maguire, with Pochettino expected to retain a three-man defence alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martinez.

In attack, the absence of Cunha could open the door for either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee, while captain Bruno Fernandes is set to face Sporting for the first time since leaving the club in January 2020. Fernandes scored 64 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting and has contributed 21 goals in 29 Champions League matches during his career.

Sporting enter the match with greater stability, better form and significantly stronger defensive foundations than their visitors. Fonseca has made a positive start in Lisbon, while the hosts continue to score regularly both domestically and in Europe.

Manchester United are desperately in need of a morale-boosting result, but their defensive issues have shown little sign of improvement and they now face one of the most consistent attacking sides in Portugal. With Sporting boasting strong Champions League form and United struggling badly away from home, the hosts appear well positioned to collect another important three points.

#1756. Manchester United get penalty review after Liverpool rout as new Leny Yoro verdict revealed

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes a red card for Leny Yoro during Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool was the correct decision - claiming it “would’ve been a surprise” if the defender wasn’t sent off.

Man Utd informed the Football Association (FA) on Monday afternoon of their intention to appeal Yoro’s three-game suspension.

After just eight minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of United at Anfield, Yoro found himself scrambling to get back after Matthijs de Ligt allowed Alexander Isak through on goal.

Chasing both man and ball, Yoro clipped Isak on the edge of the area - prompting referee Sam Barrott to show a straight red card. At the time Pochettino was spotted aggressively waving his finger, clearly disagreeing with the decision.

But on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch panel, Gallagher couldn’t see any mitigating factors for Yoro.

He said: “If you look at it from the referee's angle, is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes.

“I think most people would've expected a red card. It would've been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.”

United fans pointed out that goalkeeper Senne Lammens appeared to be reaching the loose ball before Isak, potentially changing the foul from a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Asked if he thought that Lammens would have gotten to the ball first, Gallagher replied: "I don't know. You watch it play out. That happens. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card.”

Gallagher’s fellow pundit, former England striker Jay Bothroyd, was in agreement. "It has to be a red,” he said.

“I will say, I'm not sure Isak can get a shot off, but I think he could touch the ball. It's not an obvious goalscoring opportunity, but you don't know. You have to judge if it's a foul, so you have to give the red card.

“Technically, he is in control of the ball because he touched it in that direction. It's if he's heavy or not."

Ex-Tottenham manager Tim Sherwood was less certain. He said: "I think if he hadn't been given a red he could've gotten away with it by saying Isak wasn't in control of the ball. I think I can listen to both sides.

"You have to assess where Lammens was. The ball was nearly in his hands."

There was further frustration for United on Merseyside, with Pochettino believing that his side should have been awarded a penalty in the first half.

Bryan Mbeumo found himself barged off the ball by Jeremy Jacquet inside the box, but the entire panel rejected those claims.

Gallagher explained: “When players are side by side, you can do that. They are side by side. Jacquet was even in front of him."

Bothroyd concurred: "If I am Pochettino, I am telling Mbeumo to get in the gym. That is just strength."

Sherwood agreed, admiring Jacquet. He concluded: "No penalty. How good is he by the way, Jacquet?"

#1753. Rio Ngumoha breaks Premier League record in Liverpool win vs Man Utd

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 18:54, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 19:40

Liverpool produced arguably their finest performance under Andoni Iraola as they thrashed Manchester United 4-0 in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

The victory keeps the Reds third in the Premier League table, but they have closed the gap on Manchester City to one point and remain seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, the Red Devils were reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Alexander Isak.

From the resulting free kick, Dominik Szoboszlai fired Liverpool into the lead, before the hosts strengthened their advantage when Florian Wirtz finished off a brilliant move down the flank involving Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds youngster got on the scoresheet himself in the second half, while substitute Victor Munoz put the finishing touches on a commanding display by netting the fourth goal.

With Cody Gakpo unavailable, Iraola handed Ngumoha a place in the starting lineup, and the youngster delivered an electrifying performance on the night.

According to Opta Joe, Ngumoha became the youngest player ever to register a goal involvement in a Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Picking up possession, he bamboozled his marker before whipping in a superb left-footed cross, which Wirtz emphatically converted to put Liverpool 2-0 ahead.

After the break, Bradley Barcola escaped his marker and played a perfectly weighted pass into Ngumoha's path, leaving the youngster with a simple finish.

In doing so, Ngumoha also became the youngest player to score and provide an assist in a Premier League match since Michael Owen achieved the feat on Boxing Day 1997.

Reports have emerged in recent weeks suggesting that Bayern Munich remain interested in signing Ngumoha, but Liverpool should not entertain any offers for the highly-rated youngster.

Ngumoha is already receiving more opportunities under Iraola and is expected to play a significant role this season.

Liverpool rate him highly, and there is little doubt that he could develop into a regular first-team fixture as he continues to mature.

While Yoro's dismissal certainly helped Liverpool take control of the contest, Man Utd offered little to trouble the hosts and failed to frustrate them by remaining resolute at the back.

#1751. World Cup returns to United Kingdom for first time since 1966 as FIFA name host stadia

The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be hosted jointly by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, FIFA have confirmed, with the tournament returning to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966.

The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

The bid has put forward 19 potential venues, including five in London: Wembley Stadium, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Emirates, Stamford Bridge and a renovated Selhurst Park. Old Trafford will be considered, regardless of whether Manchester United moves to its proposed new home.

Some 32 teams will contest the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, but this is due to expand to 48 from 2031 onwards. The tournament, then, will comprise 104 matches.

England has not hosted a major tournament since staging the women’s European Championships in 2022, which the Lionesses won. It has failed in bids to host the 2006 and 2018 men’s World Cups. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the Men’s European Championship in 2028.

It is understood that the process of finalising the list of stadia that will be used is ongoing and is under FIFA’s jurisdiction. Wembley is the only stadium that currently meets the standards required to host the World Cup final.

Burnham calls for ambition after ‘deeply disappointing’ Cop31 disagreements

Disability benefits: Who receives them and what do they cost the Government?

South East Water slumps to loss after hefty bill from supply failures

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

The 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential new Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

“Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”

FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

#1750. Mauricio Pochettino suffers unwanted Premier League first in Man Utd loss vs Liverpool

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 19:24

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United reign got off to a disastrous start as the Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Argentine took charge of the club earlier this week after Man Utd parted ways with Michael Carrick, leaving him with barely a few days to work with his new players on the training ground.

Pochettino had won just three of his previous 19 games before Sunday's encounter, and the final whistle brought no improvement to that record.

The defeat also had a damaging impact on the league standings, with Man Utd dropping to 19th in the Premier League table on eight points after 11 matches, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

According to Opta Joe, Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

The game was only eight minutes old when the Man Utd backline was caught napping, forcing Leny Yoro into a challenge on Alexander Isak that resulted in a red card.

Liverpool capitalised on United's defensive frailties, scoring twice before the break through Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz.

The hosts enjoyed greater control after the interval and added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the former also setting a Premier League record of his own.

Pochettino also entered the Man Utd history books for the wrong reasons, suffering the joint-heaviest defeat by any Red Devils manager in his first game in charge, matching Lal Hilditch's 4-0 loss against Bolton Wanderers in October 1926.

Considering Man Utd's struggles so far this season, the defeat against Liverpool need not spell the end of the world for the Red Devils or their new manager.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to collect as many points as possible and create some breathing space between his side and the teams at the bottom of the table.

There were precious few positives to take from the performance, aside from Senne Lammens's display, but Pochettino will hope to see greater improvement from his players in the coming days.

#1749. De Zerbi claims Marseille used him as ‘scapegoat’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto De Zerbi accused former club Marseille of using him as a "scapegoat" despite him giving "everything" for them.

De Zerbi took charge of Marseille in June 2024 on a three-year contract and led them to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 in his debut campaign.

He also came within seconds of winning the Trophee des Champions in the following campaign, but Goncalo Ramos scored a 95th-minute equaliser for Paris Saint-Germain to take the game to penalties, and Marseille lost the shootout.

De Zerbi's tenure did not last much longer after that; a Champions League league-phase exit was followed by a 5-0 Classique hammering, which resulted in his departure in February.

The Italian was not out of a job for long, signing with Tottenham at the end of March, but he has now hit out at Marseille for what he feels was unjust treatment.

"Many times, I was the scapegoat for everyone, but in such an important club and city, everyone has to take responsibility, not just a few people, of whom I was one," De Zerbi told Canal+, as quoted by TNT Sports.

"I'm sorry, because when I signed for Marseille, I wanted it so badly and I thought I would stay for many years.

"However, some people didn't keep their word to me. They told me things they didn't follow through on. A year and a half had passed before the Champions Trophy in Kuwait.

"We were on the verge of winning a title after a 12-year drought. Since that match, the situation deteriorated; it worsened until my departure.

"Marseille is one of the clubs I hold closest to my heart, along with Foggia. I suffered a lot when I left. I suffered because I gave everything in Marseille."

Moving forward as one https://t.co/NSYHCeV5Wp

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 21, 2026

De Zerbi has impressed since arriving at Spurs, ensuring they kept their Premier League status on the last day of the 2025-26 season.

Though they failed to win their first six Premier League games this term, they have since lost just one of their last five (W4) to move them up to ninth in the table.

However, he has admitted he does not see himself remaining in coaching for a long time, as he is keen to explore life outside of football, though he is in no hurry to leave the dugout just yet.

"I don't think I'll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn't just that," he added.

"That time hasn't come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream.

"I don't measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have. I always want to stay the same and always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them."

#1748. Amorim discusses ‘fun’ Frosinone, final third struggles and confirms Pavlovic’s return

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your plan. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”

#1747. Manchester United XI vs Sporting: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Champions League

Mauricio Pochettino will be hoping to put his nightmare Manchester United debut behind him when he takes his new side to Portugal to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The Argentine endured a horror start to his tenure at Old Trafford with a heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The Red Devils were down to ten men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity.

United suffered no injury blows on Merseyside, but the result was “painful” according to their new head coach, and he will be looking to put things right immediately in Europe’s top competition on Wednesday.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with his inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI at Anfield, with the Dutchman having been sidelined for over a year with a persistent back injury.

The centre-half looked awkward for much of the match, and his selection was scrutinised intensely afterwards.

It remains to be seen whether he will play again here, with Harry Maguire introduced in the first half and shoring up United’s back five.

The England international should start here, perhaps alongisde Yoro, who will not be suspended for this match with his ban only for league games.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged at left-back once more, although the Argentine had to shift back inside after Yoro’s red card, with Dorgu shifting back to wing-back from his left wing berth.

Diogo Dalot failed to truly impress on Merseyside and could see himself rotated for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the sending-off as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should get the nod here.

#1746. Bruno Guimaraes reveals Arsenal ‘apology’ after £75m transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Bruno Guimaraes revealed he apologised to the Arsenal squad after joining the club in the summer.

The Brazilian spent five years at Newcastle before completing a £75million move to Arsenal in August.

During his time on Tyneside, Guimaraes had several heated clashed with Arsenal’s midfielders, including Jorginho and Declan Rice.

Once he had switched loyalties and become a Gunner, the No39 addressed those battles with his new team-mates.

“I remember the first time I had to speak in front of everyone, the first thing I said was sorry to the boys.” Guimaraes said.

“Because definitely, [those] who knows me know how much I hate to lose. I always play hard and I know I have some fights against them.

“So I say sorry now [we’re] in the same team, ‘I can’t wait to compete for you guys’.”

It has been a patchy start to life at Arsenal for Guimaraes, who has had his best moments off the bench as a substitute.

He has struggled more when starting and his partnership with Rice has not looked a particularly balanced or natural one.

However, the 29-year-old insisted there is still “much more” to come from him, and he is determined to play his part in an Arsenal side challenging on all fronts.

“We push each other to always be playing well, because if you don’t play well, other players will come and play well,” Guimaraes said.

“I think that’s very important for Arsenal. We want to make a dynasty here; we want to win everything possible. I think since I came to the club, the first thing Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club, so we want to win everything that’s possible.

“I know how much the Champions League means for the fans, and for us here. Tomorrow we have a big test with a top team, they have been unbelievable this season, so tomorrow we have to play a very good game because it’s going to be against a top side.”

#1745. De Bruyne not focused on Napoli exit rumours ahead of Man City reunion

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Kevin De Bruyne insisted the "unpleasant" rumours surrounding his future at Napoli would be put to one side ahead of his return to Manchester City on Tuesday.

De Bruyne returns to the Etihad Stadium for the second straight season for another Champions League encounter, but the Belgian has been the subject of speculation.

It has been reported that the 35-year-old, who only joined the Serie A giants from Man City last summer, could be on his way out as early as the January transfer window.

PSV has been touted as a possible destination for De Bruyne, with the midfielder out of contract at the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

De Bruyne's wife revealed in a recent magazine interview that she would one day like to return to Belgium, though De Bruyne said her words were misinterpreted by the Italian media and was keen to put the record straight.

"I'm quite sorry about it all, to be honest. If you go and read the article which you have not read, you will understand what she said," De Bruyne told reporters.

"I was away in Belgium and then a lot of things were being said and there were a lot of negative reactions towards my wife.

"I saw photos of my house in the press, which is not good. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don't know why.

"You do not know my private life, you have no right to comment on my private life. It was an unpleasant situation for me and my wife."

When pressed further on his future in Naples, De Bruyne added: "I can't say very much at this point. I've played at 400% so far.

"I'm not 20 years old anymore, I'm almost 36, so there are lots of things to consider.

"Right now, there's not a lot to say. I'm playing well, I'm trying to help the team to do well. There have been lots of challenges this year and a lot of things have happened."

Squad for Manchester City v Napoli https://t.co/E9kZvZPQTj

— Official SSC Napoli (@en_sscnapoli) November 23, 2026

De Bruyne will be hoping to play a bigger part in Napoli's next trip to his former employers, having been substituted early on following Giovanni Di Lorenzo's red card.

City won 2-0 that day thanks to goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku, with City unbeaten at home against Napoli (W2 D1).

De Bruyne was directly involved in 41 goals in 72 Champions League appearances for City (16 goals, 25 assists), the joint second-most for the club along with Haaland (41 in 42 games), with the pair only trailing Sergio Aguero (43).

He registered 108 goals and provided 170 assists in 422 appearances in all competitions during a trophy-laden spell with City.

City were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009-10 and 2017-18 in September, and they have since appealed the ruling. With the appeal still ongoing, the potential punishments should the verdict be upheld have not been revealed.

"This is my club, I love the owners. I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change," De Bruyne said of City's situation.

"Of course, in life there are rules, everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I play between the white lines and I compete with other players and I have had a lot of experiences with my teams, with the players, so for me that is the thing that I value most.

"And even later on in my career, I think the most important is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

"I've given my all and that is not going to change in my mind I don't think. Other people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played but everybody has their own opinion I guess."

#1744. Galatasaray vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 22 Nov 2026 19:53

Galatasaray will be looking to continue their resurgence in the UEFA Champions League when they welcome Aston Villa to Rams Park on Tuesday evening, with the Turkish champions aiming to close the gap on the top eight.

The hosts sit 18th in the league-phase standings with six points from four matches, while Villa occupy sixth place on nine points and will be looking to return to winning ways after a difficult run of results.

Galatasaray head into this fixture in encouraging form after winning seven consecutive matches across all competitions, with their recent improvement helping them maintain their position at the top of the Turkish Super Lig while also strengthening their Champions League qualification prospects.

Okan Buruk's side have won their last two UCL matches, recording a 4-2 victory away to Lille before following that result with a 2-0 home triumph over VfB Stuttgart.x

The victories helped steady the ship after Galatasaray had suffered defeats against Sporting CP and Barcelona in their opening two Champions League fixtures, leaving them with little margin for error in their pursuit of a place in the knockout stages.

They have also continued their impressive run domestically, winning their last six league matches, a run that includes a win over Fenerbahce, and most recently a 2-1 win over Samsunspor 2-1 at the weekend.

Galatasaray have also been particularly impressive at home this season, winning seven of their nine matches at Rams Park while drawing one and losing one, with Barcelona the only side to defeat them on their own turf.

They will now have the opportunity to equal their best-ever run of consecutive victories in the European Cup or Champions League by recording a third straight success.

However, their defensive record remains a concern, having conceded nine goals in their opening four Champions League matches, including four in their home defeat against Barcelona and two against Lille.

Meanwhile, Villa arrive in Istanbul having experienced a significant dip in form, with their five-game winless run following a period during which they were without defeat in eight straight games, winning seven of those matches.

Unai Emery's side began that difficult sequence with a 3-0 loss away to Bournemouth in the League Cup, before subsequently drawing 1-1 with Fulham, which preceded a disappointing result in the Champions League as they lost 3-0 away to Barcelona.

Villa then produced an entertaining but defensively concerning performance in a 4-4 draw against Manchester United, before a goalless draw with Sunderland in their last outing.

Nevertheless, Villa have made an encouraging start to their Champions League campaign, winning three of their opening four matches to collect nine points and remain among the teams occupying the automatic qualification positions.

Their European campaign has included a particularly impressive 6-0 victory against Fenerbahce, which represented their widest margin of victory in European competition against a Turkish opponent, and they will be eager to rediscover that level of performance in Istanbul.

Both teams have never met in competitive football, making Tuesday's encounter the first meeting between the sides, although the hosts have traditionally proved difficult opponents for English clubs playing in Istanbul.

English teams have failed to win in nine of their last 10 visits to Galatasaray, losing six and drawing three, while Villa have lost just once in eight European matches against Turkish opposition, winning six and drawing one.

Galatasaray are expected to be without Victor Osimhen, who underwent knee surgery after sustaining an injury during their Champions League victory over Stuttgart.

Rafael Leao is also sidelined with a muscle injury, while Roland Sallai and Ismail Jakobs are carrying fitness concerns and could miss Tuesday's encounter.

Aleksey Batrakov, who has scored four goals in the Champions League this season, three of which have been at RAMS Park, will be the man to watch in Osimhen’s absence.

Villa will be without Matty Cash, who sustained a concussion while on international duty with Poland, while Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri are also expected to remain sidelined through injury.

Victor Lindelof is a doubt after missing the weekend draw against Sunderland due to illness, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka has returned from a hamstring problem and could be available for selection.

Nicolas Jackson is expected to lead the attack, with John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Johan Manzambi likely to provide support as Emery looks to end Villa's winless run.

Cakir; Singo, Sanchez, Bardakci, Elmali; Torreira, Lemina; Akgun, Batrakov, Yilmaz; Gul

Suzuki; Bogarde, Harwood-Bellis, Pau Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Joao Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Manzambi; Jackson

Galatasaray have been in impressive form in recent weeks and their home performances should give them confidence of securing another positive result against Villa.

However, the hosts will be without several important attacking players potentially limiting their options in the final third, and while Villa have struggled defensively during their recent winless run, they have enough in attack to play out an entertaining draw in Istanbul.

#1743. Emmanuel Emegha: New details emerge as Chelsea striker ‘robbed’ after Leeds game

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was “robbed” following Saturday’s Premier League match against Leeds.

Sources close to the Dutchman say that while his phone was not among the possessions stolen, personal belongings and several work-related items were taken. The incident took place outside a hotel in Mayfair on Saturday night.

Emegha was unhurt, with Chelsea understood to be aware of the situation and providing their full support to the player.

The Metropolitan Police are also aware of the situation.

Emegha scored against Leeds on what was his first Premier League start for Chelsea since arriving from BlueCo sister club Strasbourg in the summer, but his goal made little difference in the end as Leeds won 4-1 against Xabi Alonso’s side.

The 23-year-old took to Instagram on Sunday evening to reveal that he had been robbed in London shortly after the match.

“Unfortunately after the game I was robbed,” Emegha wrote. “I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”

The post started: “First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday [against Nottingham Forest].”

Emegha’s transfer to Chelsea was agreed in September 2025 but he remained at Strasbourg last season and arrived at Stamford Bridge in the summer.

He scored 31 goals in 78 total appearances for Strasbourg across all competitions and opened his account for Chelsea on his third outing.

After nursing a hamstring injury at the beginning of the season, he made his first competitive appearance off the bench in Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month before then being handed a league debut in the 1-0 loss at Sunderland before the international break.

#1741. The Chelsea problem Xabi Alonso cannot ignore - and who is really to blame

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

There is no defending Chelsea, because again there was simply no defending by Chelsea.

One goal up and with home advantage against a Leeds team they had already beaten at Stamford Bridge this season in the Carabao Cup, Xabi Alonso and his players took that encouraging platform for success and ripped it up, deservedly losing 4-1.

At least Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United could play the “we only had 10 men” card.

Whatever is failing to function right now at Chelsea is a complex web spun by poor decision-making and performances from a whole host of implicated parties.

The Chelsea defence showcases the Blues’ endemic struggles for consistency in a perfect microcosmic form, not least because there are so many stakeholders who must each accept their share of the blame.

An injury record peculiarly problematic for a team largely only playing once a week this season in the absence of any European football has left them without captain Reece James, summer signing Maxence Lacroix and the improved Jorrel Hato - players whose availability might not cure all their defensive ills, but would certainly help.

Their absences mean more minutes for players not showing any signs that they possess the composure or robustness needed to provide support for a potent attack and secure a return to the Champions League.

Malo Gusto was beaten twice for Brenden Aaronson’s run to goal for Leeds’ fourth - something that happens all too often for a player valued by Chelsea at £75million in the summer transfer market.

Wesley Fofana remains a liability, and his £75m transfer fee back in 2022 - £89.2m adjusted for inflation - surely makes him the worst pound-for-pound signing Chelsea have made in the BlueCo era.

And while Josh Acheampong, 20, has been the one Chelsea defender to draw consistent praise in the first three months of the campaign, he was suspect against Leeds.

So too was Levi Colwill, a player with enormous potential but who has so far failed to rediscover his physicality and form since the torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for almost all of last season.

A question it is worth Alonso and his coaching staff asking themselves: is 34-year-old Emi Martinez clearly a better goalkeeper than Mike Penders, the inevitable long-term No1?

New details emerge as Chelsea star ‘robbed’ after Leeds game

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move; Man Utd striker deal

Chelsea get new Rogers penalty review after Leeds handball controversy

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

There is a case to be made to fully blood Penders now, whatever promises might have been made to Martinez when he joined. The Argentine currently looks a shadow of the commanding player he was at Aston Villa.

Wesley Fofana must surely be Chelsea’s worst pound-for-pound signing in the BlueCo era

Individual errors from Fofana and Gusto and the softness of Colwill and Martinez mean plenty of the blame is rightly being portioned in their direction, but other parties are just as culpable.

Alonso, for example, has flattered to deceive as manager so far, switching between a back three and a back four with the result that his team look capable of playing neither, not both. His Chelsea side have scored a laudable 20 league goals but conceded a lamentable 20 at the other end.

Responsibility also lies at the boardroom door, where questionable recruitment has taken place. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi were not at the standard required and have taken too long to move on (still neither player has permanently left the club).

And while he is far from the complete product, Trevoh Chalobah had been one of the more consistent centre-backs of the Clearlake era yet was moved on to high-flying Como this summer in favour of handing a greater amount of game time to Fofana.

If Chelsea are to get back to the pinnacle of English football, which is where the club sees itself, then recruitment, coaching and player performances must all improve.

Accepting shared responsibility is the first step towards revamping and properly rebuilding a defence that simply isn’t going to deliver Champions League football on current form.
