#1723. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#1722. Arena aiming to make home advantage count in San Jose’s playoff opener

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bruce Arena insisted the San Jose Earthquakes must use the PayPal Park atmosphere to their advantage in their MLS Cup Playoff opener against the Houston Dynamo.

San Jose are back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023 after a strong regular season that saw them finish fourth in the Western Conference, one point clear of Houston.

The Earthquakes have won just one of their last seven MLS games (D4 L2) and enter the postseason on the back of a 3-1 loss to Minnesota United.

And their record on home soil has not been the best in 2026. San Jose won just seven matches in front of their own supporters in the league, the fifth-lowest tally in the West.

Arena, however, believes the San Jose supporters have a big role to play when Houston visit for Game 1 of their best-of-three series.

"Making the playoffs was our goal, and we achieved that," said Arena. "Now it's going to be important to get a big crowd for the first game against Houston.

"Home-field advantage means something, so if we can get the support from the stands and play well on the field, hopefully that produces a win."

there’s nothing like a home playoff match this is what we play for. this is who we play for. the kind of atmosphere you have to experience for yourself. https://t.co/z3McgjIpfq

— San Jose Earthquakes (@SJEarthquakes) November 22, 2026

Houston, meanwhile, signed off for the playoffs with back-to-back defeats, including a Decision Day loss against St. Louis City SC, with Lukas MacNaughton netting a late winner.

But when it comes to the playoffs, the Dynamo have great pedigree. Only three teams have won back-to-back MLS Cup titles, including the 2006-07 Houston side.

The Dynamo also reached the MLS Cup final in 2011 and 2012, but were beaten by the LA Galaxy on both occasions, with the team out for revenge 15 years later.

They have already won the 2023 U.S. Open Cup under head coach Ben Olsen, and now could tie the Columbus Crew (three) for the third-most titles in league history.

Judd was the key to San Jose's offence this season, scoring 17 goals in the MLS regular season.

No Earthquakes player has scored more in a single regular season since Chris Wondolowski scored 27 in 2012.

Houston built its season on a strong defence, which can be highlighted by Halter’s tackle success rate.

Of Dynamo players who played a minimum of 1000 minutes, no player was more successful in their tackles, as he recorded a tackle success rate of 73.1%.

"A winning mentality, hungry for winning titles. To be able to make history for this club." It's the playoffs. The mentality has shifted. The energy has shifted. The focus has shifted. We're hungry for more. https://t.co/SJ7qpmS97C

— Houston Dynamo FC (@HoustonDynamo) November 21, 2026

MATCH PREDICTION: SAN JOSE EARTHQUAKES WIN

San Jose and Houston have never met in the MLS Cup playoffs but have played 37 regular-season matches, with the Dynamo leading the series with 19 wins to San Jose's 12 (six draws).

The Earthquakes are, however, currently on a four-game undefeated streak against the Dynamo (W2 D2), having not lost since 2024, setting up an intriguing encounter.

It is the first time since 2023 that San Jose have qualified for the playoffs. They have advanced past Round One only once since returning to the MLS in 2008, knocking out New York Red Bulls in 2010.

Houston, meanwhile, are making their first appearance in the playoffs since 2024, coming in with a record of W18 D11 L11 in the postseason.

Their last playoff win came against Sporting Kansas City in 2023, and they have since managed a record of W0 D2 L1.

#1721. Why isn’t Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund on TNT Sports tonight?

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League this evening, but it will not be shown on TNT Sports, as is usually the case for European football in the UK.

The Gunners go into this game looking to get back to winning ways after a surprise draw with Newcastle at St James’ Park, where the north Londoners were given an almighty scare.

Noni Madueke netted a late equaliser for the Premier League champions, who had fallen behind after Malick Thiaw bundled home from a set piece after Harvey Barnes had cancelled out Eberechi Eze’s opener.

They take on a Dortmund side that are top of the Bundesliga after 10 matches, and they are two points ahead of Klassiker rivals Bayern Munich.

Amongst Niko Kovac’s cohort is Ethan Nwaneri, who is on loan at the German side from Arsenal, and he is eligible to face his parent club tonight due to Champions League rules permitting loan players to be available to face the teams they are contracted to.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund will not be broadcast live in the UK on TNT Sports. That is because under the current Champions League rights agreement on these shores, Amazon Prime Video has the first pick of one Tuesday night fixture to show exclusively on their platform up until the semi-finals.

This week they have chosen the encounter at the Emirates Stadium, which kicks off at 8pm GMT at Old Trafford. Coverage on Amazon begins at 6:30pm, hosted by Gabby Logan.

Amazon’s current arrangement will continue from 2027-2031 as per the terms of the next Champions League TV rights deal, which will see the bulk of matches head to US streaming giants Paramount in an agreement struck in 2025 worth well over £1billion.

Highlights will remain on the BBC, with Sky Sports buying the rights to show all Europa League and Conference League games in the UK from next season.

#1720. Kroupi’s preferred destination ‘revealed’ as Bournemouth rule out January sale

By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 21:24

Barcelona may be ahead in the race for Eli Junior Kroupi, according to French outlet Foot Sur7, which reports that the 20-year-old Bournemouth forward would favour the Catalan club if he decides to leave the Premier League. Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal are also following the striker’s situation, but for now they are said to be behind Barcelona in the player’s preference.

According to Foot Sur7, Kroupi has a special interest in playing for Barcelona, a possibility that had already been considered behind the scenes at the club. Barcelona’s football department has followed the striker’s development since the last summer transfer window, and his name remains on sporting director Deco’s radar as an option to strengthen the attack in the coming years.

The Catalan interest also gains strength from information given by David Ornstein this week. Speaking on The Athletic FC podcast, the British journalist said the Frenchman is weighing up leaving English football when he feels the time has come for a new step in his career. A departure from the Premier League would put Barcelona and PSG in a favourable position, particularly if English rivals lose ground in the race.

There is still no decision on the striker’s future, however. The preference for Barcelona reported by the French press does not mean a transfer is under way or that the player has made a final choice.

While Barcelona appear an attractive destination, Bournemouth are set to make any short-term move difficult. The English club are not planning to lose one of their main players in the January window and consider his presence important for their sporting goals.

The position was reinforced by boss Marco Rose, who ruled out selling the forward in January. ‘For us, it is not a plan to sell someone in January,’ Rose said. ‘It is not our plan and so far there are just rumours and noises.’

Kroupi’s contract with Bournemouth also stands in the way of suitors. The striker is under contract until June 2030, which puts the Cherries in a comfortable position. With no need to release him immediately, they can set high conditions before opening talks. According to estimates in the British press, Bournemouth could ask for close to £100m to accept a transfer. That figure is a considerable barrier, particularly for Barcelona, who would need to weigh up the financial impact of an operation of this size.

The interest is not explained solely by competition among European giants. At 20, Kroupi is already one of the most talked-about young names on the market, driven by his goalscoring ability, his versatility in attack and the room for improvement he still has. Those characteristics help explain why the Frenchman fits the profile Barcelona are seeking. The Catalan hierarchy are looking for alternatives who can add quality to the attack in the medium term, and the Bournemouth player has attributes that attract Deco and other members of the football department.

PSG are also seen as a possible heavyweight rival, especially if the striker leaves English football. Arsenal are monitoring the situation, although according to Foot Sur7 they are behind Barcelona in Kroupi’s preference.

A decision is not expected immediately. The striker intends to focus on recovering his best form this season before making any decision about a change of club, so next summer is the most likely time for a concrete assessment of his future.

With the January transfer window approaching, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham are among the clubs expected to pursue major signings. Arsenal have been linked with a surprise move for Jamal Musiala and could also seek a goalkeeper following David Raya’s injury. The Gunners face competition from Paris Saint-Germain for Eli Junior Kroupi and are reportedly interested in Tornike Kvaratskhelia, brother of Khvicha.

Manchester United are tipped to target Ivan Toney, while Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly keen on Fulham defender Calvin Bassey. Chelsea could pursue Alex Scott and Lamine Camara to strengthen midfield, with both the Blues and Arsenal linked with Cesc Fabregas as a potential managerial candidate.

Liverpool are reportedly interested in Real Madrid’s Endrick, while Tottenham are said to have agreed a new deal with teenager Luca Williams-Barnett. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Arsenal have begun talks with RB Leipzig over signing winger Antonio Nusa in a deal which could be worth £67million.

Sky Germany reports that Bayern Munich are weighing up a move for Schalke 04 goalkeeper Loris Karius.

However, the 33-year-old says he hasn’t spoken to anyone about a potential transfer.

Diario Sport claims that Barcelona now face competition from Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City for FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad.

Barca have been leading the race for the 18-year-old, but Twente’s asking price of over €20million could complicate a January move.

Wilson left the Gunners as part of the club’s overhaul of their medical department, with significant changes made in an attempt to address the injury problems that have hindered the squad in recent seasons.

Bournemouth’s Scott has become their No1 target amid a fierce transfer battle with Liverpool, while both clubs are also said to retain an interest in Camara.

TEAMtalk report that Chelsea have not ruled signing both players in January.

Manchester United are said to be pondering a January move for Ivan Toney.

The England striker is believed to be keen on returning to the Premier League in 2027 after a year-and-a-half in Saudi Arabia with Al-Ahli.

Several clubs are said to be interested in Toney, with Football Insider stating that Manchester United are being kept closely informed of the situation.

TEAMtalk claim that Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham and Crystal Palace have also been made aware of the availability of the former Brentford frontman, who could be signed on an initial loan deal that includes an option to buy.

Arsenal have a long-term interest in Jamal Musiala, reports claim.

Musiala’s Bayern Munich future has been thrown into doubt of late as he receives ongoing treatment for a neurological dysfunction that saw him faint twice during pre-season friendlies over the summer.

He has only played once since September 18 due to a muscle injury, leading to suggestions that Bayern no longer view his substantial wages as feasible amid public criticism from global players’ union FIFPRO.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal and Liverpool both hold a long-standing interest in Musiala, with Chelsea also linked with his services in the past.

#1716. Who really won AFCON 2025? When CAS will release Morocco vs Senegal verdict

The chaotic saga of litigation which followed the 2025 AFCON final will finally be resolved this week, as the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prepares to release its final decision.

The champion of AFCON 2025 remains in dispute after the now infamous events of January 18th, where Senegal were stripped of a 1-0 victory after their squad briefly left the pitch in the second half.

An unprecedented and unsavoury series of events followed. Morocco appealed the result and won, before Senegal escalated the affair to CAS in Lausanne, the world’s premier body for the resolution of sporting disputes.

Now, ten months after the full-time whistle was blown in Rabat, AFCON 2025 will finally have an undisputed champion, though the animosity will surely remain, regardless of the verdict.

Here is everything you need to know about the situation ahead of the final verdict being released...

An official press release from CAS confirms the decision will be released on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

No specific time of day has been set. The press release simply says the decision will be released “in the course of the afternoon.”

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In March 2026, two months after the final, CAF announced the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch.

The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco, who are now considered the AFCON 2025 champions.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) immediately hit back at CAF’s decision to strip them of the AFCON title, and have since refused to return the trophy, which they have regularly paraded in public.

The FSF immediately appealed CAF’s decision and the case fell to CAS. CAF president Patrice Motsepe acknowledged Senegal’s “right” to do so and added that he will “respect the decision that’s taken at the highest level.”

The government of Senegal has also criticised CAF’s move, expressing “profound dismay” and questioning the governing body’s credibility.

The Moroccan football federation, meanwhile, has called for tournament rules to be “respected” as they maintain their status as champions.

#1715. AC Milan Women 3-2 Sassuolo: Grimshaw crucial after crazy first half

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

#1714. Andrews’ ‘ambitious’ changes pay off in Brentford’s thrashing of Everton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday showed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.

Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted twice in the space of 178 seconds in the first half to put the Bees in control before Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off in the 40th minute.

Tarkowski was dismissed for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk high on his shin after clearing the ball, with referee Craig Pawson overruling his original decision after a VAR review.

Vitaly Janelt's 67th-minute thunderbolt was the pick of Brentford's goals, with substitute Fabio Carvalho climbing off the bench to add further gloss to the scoreline late on.

Brentford enjoyed their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League, equalling their 4-0 rout of Manchester United in August 2022, with their display coming after Andrews elected to make four changes to the side that were beaten by Brighton.

Callum Wilson replaced the suspended Igor Thiago up front, while Yarmoliuk, Mikkel Damsgaard and Jaidon Anthony all came in to replace Mamadou Sangare and Kevin Schade, while Aaron Hickey missed out all together through injury.

"Big impact, it's the nature of the game and the squad. We have the luxury of choosing from very good players," Andrews told Sky Sports on the reason behind his alterations.

"Some will be disappointed not to play more, but the reality is we need everybody. We want to be ambitious, so we need everybody. The boys that came in did really well."

After missing out on European football last season, Brentford's win saw them climb up to sixth in the Premier League and just four points adrift of fourth-place Liverpool.

"We know what the other side feels like, but I wanted to keep our habits, be professional, try to control the game and wait for the right openings," Andrews added.

"Each game is very different, very difficult. The expectation levels at this club have changed and, regardless of the performance, the win to go sixth in the league and still questions about 'should they be doing better?' – I think people need to get real.

"I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it."

Since Andrews took charge of Brentford ahead of the 2025-26 season, of London clubs, only Arsenal (113) have won more Premier League points than the Bees (70).

Brentford also hit the 300-goal mark in the Premier League in their 201st game in the competition (303 goals in total), the fifth-fastest side to do so, after Man United (165), Newcastle United (170), Liverpool (190) and Blackburn Rovers (191).

Lewis-Potter got the landmark goal, and in 11 appearances this season, he has already beaten his best-ever scoring season in the Premier League (three in 36 apps in 2025-26 and 3 in 30 in 2023-24), with his double taking him to four this term.

"He's been excellent, growing all the time since I've been here," Andrews said of Lewis-Potter.

"Finds himself in unnatural positions – we give him the freedom to go and roam, and he's proving very difficult for the opposition to mark."

#1713. Arsenal XI vs Borussia Dortmund: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news and injury latest for Champions League

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba is in contention to make his first Arsenal start of the season against Borussia Dortmund, as Mikel Arteta also faces a tricky decision over who starts in goal.

The French defender had a long spell on the sidelines after aggravating a back injury at the World Cup over the summer.

Saliba did not require surgery but a significant period of rest was needed and he is yet to play a single first-team minute so far this season.

He played the first half for Arsenal’s Under-21s in their PL2 win over Aston Villa before the international break and then featured in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Watford.

Having come through those games without any issues, Saliba is in contention for a first-team return and he could be brought in against Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Goalkeeper David Raya will miss the match with a shoulder injury suffered late on during Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League and deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to start in his place, over Illan Meslier.

Ben White could get the nod at right-back, as he continues to share minutes with Jurrien Timber, while Myles Lewis-Skelly will hope to get his opportunity in midfield.

Arsenal have a huge Premier League match at home to Manchester City to come on Sunday but Bundesliga leaders Dortmund represent tough opposition and manager Mikel Arteta is likely to go strong with his team selection.

That would mean more minutes in midfield for Declan Rice and captain Martin Odegaard, with Martin Zubimendi still sidelined, while Noni Madueke has become an essential part of the attack on the right wing in the absence of Bukayo Saka.

Up front, Viktor Gyokeres' chances to start have largely come in the Champions League this season and it would be no surprise if he was chosen to lead the line against Dortmund, ahead of Kai Havertz.

#1709. Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes fumes in unseen interview amid new Leny Yoro red card verdict

Bruno Fernandes laid into the standard of Premier League referees after Manchester United were beaten by Liverpool at the weekend.

The Red Devils played most of the match with ten men after Leny Yoro was dismissed for tripping Alexander Isak, who was through on goal, and Dominik Szoboszlai powered home the opener from the resultant free kick.

Further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz consigned them to a heavy defeat on Mauricio Pochettino’s return to the Premier League, with his new club still mired in the relegation zone.

Fernandes, whose future remains up in the air with his current contract due to expire in the summer, played the full duration at Anfield and cut a frustrated figure at the full-time whistle.

Speaking post-match, he questioned referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro. Several pundits have questioned whether Isak’s heavy touch had killed his chances of scoring from the one-on-one, with debate raging for days post-match.

“I’m not complaining,” Fernandes caveated, speaking in Portuguese to ESPN Brasil. “The situation is clear from what they explain to us at the start of the season.

“I think we have far too many meetings with referees for them to explain the rules, only for the referees themselves not to know them.

“We have four officials at the game, plus another two on VAR. I understand it’s a difficult situation, but VAR can watch it again and again, with replays, slow motion, everything.

“Isak puts his leg in front of Leny simply to try to win a foul. The ball is knocked forward, towards Senne’s hands. He has absolutely no control of the ball.

“For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”

#1708. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1706. Liverpool FC: Klopp Won’t Buy Big In January, & Why It’s The Right Move

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool FC: Klopp Won't Buy Big In January, & Why It's The Right Move

Jurgen Kloppai??i??s countrymen are well versed with the appeal of quick fixes. They once allowed one of historyai??i??s most hated figures to rise to power. Of course, when Adolf Hitler was rapidly gaining popularity in Germany, he didnai??i??t do it by telling his people he would bring about the Second World War so soon after the first one had concluded. No, he did it by promising quick fixes. In a country reeling from the effects of the first World War and later the onset of the Great Depression, the promises of a party that would swoop in and fix issues ranging from more practical ones like unemployment, to rather more emotional ones like the loss of national pride after the defeat in the previous World War, was welcome to the masses.

Liverpool FC is a little like post World War I Germany — a lot of pride, but very little recent success to validate all that ego. As a result, the fans are in a constant state of impatience, always hoping the next player or the next manager will be the one to lead them back to the glory days. Thereai??i??s nothing wrong with having hope, but it needs to be balanced with practicality. Overly inflated expectations almost always tend to blow up in oneai??i??s face.

Jurgen Klopp is quite different from the former Nazi party leader of course. From day 1, heai??i??s been trying to temper expectations rather than fuel them.

a Expectations can be a really big problem. Itai??i??s like a backpack ai??i?? 20 kilos more! Iai??i??m not here to promise that against Tottenham you will see the new LFC, but maybe some of it. Everything in life takes time, the only thing nobody gives time is development.a ai??i?? Jurgen Klopp

Instead itai??i??s the fans that are overburdening the manager and the team with their dreams of an overnight turnover of fortunes. With every 4-1 against Manchester City and 6-1 rout over Southampton, the fans have responded by hailing their players footballing maestros, and their manager a genius. When these games have been inevitably followed by underwhelming performances, the same players have been declared a Brendan Rodgersai??i?? signingsa and a not worthy of wearing a Liverpool shirta . Neither of these stands is right, and there is a dire need for fans to ground themselves in reality, and really understand where the club stands.

Insanity is doing the same things over and over again and expecting different results. In the past, Liverpool have conducted mass-recruitment, spending a pretty penny in the process, and not really seen any major reversal of fortunes. So now that results have been poor in recent weeks, what do fans want? New signings of course. Ignoring the fact that squad overhauls havenai??i??t helped in the past. And ignoring the fact that Klopp does not generally delve deeply into the scouting process, hence the transfer committee is likely to be just as influential as it was during Brendan Rodgersai??i?? tenure (if not more).

The good news is that Jurgen Klopp seems far from keen to jump onto the transfer bandwagon. Heai??i??s instead decided to focus on the rich pool of players already on the teamai??i??s rolls, either on loan to other clubs or playing for the youth club. This greatly reflects his vision and ability to curb any impulse to seek a ready-made answer in the transfer market.

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

In the last two weeks, Klopp has recalled loanees Tiago Ilori (Aston Villa), Sheyi Ojo (Wolverhampton), Ryan Kent (Coventry City), Danny Ward (Aberdeen) and Kevin Stewart (Swindon Town). Against Exeter City, he also utilized all of these players barring Ward, and played youngsters Cameron Brannagan, Joao Carlos Teixeira, Jerome Sinclair, Brad Smith and Connor Randall.

This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1705. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1704. Man United transfer news: Calvin Bassey gives "negotiations" update as relegation battle makes Mauricio Pochettino desperate

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 01:54

Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations to extend his contract despite interest from Manchester United this January.

The Red Devils were resoundingly beaten by Liverpool on Sunday, losing 4-0 at Anfield, with defender Leny Yoro receiving an early red card.

Mauricio Pochettino has only been leading the club since Wednesday, but he will already be aware of the need to address the team's defensive frailties, especially as they are 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points after 11 matchweeks.

The Red Devils have been linked with centre-back Bassey, but the defender confirmed that he is in discussions to extend his deal with Fulham, telling TNT Sports: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations."

Bassey's current deal is set to expire in 2027, though Fulham have an option to extend his stay by a year, so news that the 26-year-old is hopeful of further extending his time at Craven Cottage will come as a blow to Pochettino.

“Just proud of the boys today, you know how hard it is to play here” Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber reflect on a huge point for Fulham away at the Etihad ? ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Szb8cvHyJ6

Bassey is a strong channel defender and is much more athletic than United's current options at the back, something that has been a major issue this season.

Harry Maguire is now 33 and his mobility issues have only worsened as he has aged, while Lisandro Martinez has never been suited to playing in an aggressive, high-pressing system.

Yoro is young enough to contribute in the coming seasons, but he has not developed since signing for the club in July 2024.

The Premier League is the most physically and mentally demanding league in the world, and signing someone with experience of the top flight would be hugely beneficial.

The reservations that some have at the club about Bassey's place in the XI in the years to come should not matter given the real threat of relegation.

United would have ended Sunday bottom of the league had Crystal Palace beaten Coventry City on Saturday, and the fixture schedule does not get any easier for the Red Devils.

With games against Brentford, Newcastle United, Coventry, Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland to come before the end of the year, Pochettino's side cannot afford to drop many points if they wish to avoid the one-point gap to safety increasing.
